edge_cases.description: Locate the first spike at which kernel and Brian2 part ways in seed 0 of the sugar test, read the kernel's margin to threshold there, and re-run the kernel with the rest-snapping shortcut off (eps_v = eps_g = 0) and then also with float64 state, to learn whether the one divergence is numerical (snap / float32) or a semantic mismatch.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: 'Near-threshold event' is an inference: compare_brian2.py records only counts. The kernel snaps any neuron within 0.01 mV of rest to rest (lif.py eps_v), a perturbation ~1000x larger than float32 resolution and not in Brian2; or a rare refractory/kick boundary case could be mis-handled. If the divergence survives eps=0 + float64, 'spike for spike' is not true and a semantic bug exists.
edge_cases.how_to_run: NEW CODE. (1) brain/tests/brian2_reference.py: add `--record-times` (store_true); when set use SpikeMonitor(neu) with record=True and save per seed `spk_i_<s>` = mon.i and `spk_step_<s>` = round(mon.t/ms/dt) (int64) in the output npz. (2) New brain/tests/brian2_first_divergence.py: args --conn EXPORT.npz --ref REF.npz --dt 0.1 --seeds 0 1 2 --eps-v 0.01 --eps-g 0.001 --float64 (store_true) --out JSON. Per seed: LIF(W, LIFParams(dt, w_syn=0.275*w_syn_scale, eps_v, eps_g)); if --float64 cast sim.v, sim.g, sim.buf to float64 after construction (numba compiles a float64 specialisation); first pass unrecorded to get kernel counts, record_mask = neurons spiking in either run; second pass with sim.run(1000, record_mask); compare sorted (step, neuron) event lists with Brian2's (calibrate the step offset on seed 1, where counts are identical); report identical-counts yes/no, first mismatched (step, neuron), and that neuron's kernel v for the 20 steps before (re-run deterministically to step-20, then sim.run(dt) in a loop reading sim.v[i]). Commands (project root, after the live queue finishes): `B2=$TMPDIR/flycraft_brian2` (already holds flywire_export.npz of the published model); `b2venv/bin/python brain/tests/brian2_reference.py --conn $B2/flywire_export.npz --drive in_grn_sugar:100 --ms 1000 --seeds 3 --dt 0.1 --record-times --out $B2/ref_sugar_times.npz`; then `NUMBA_CACHE_DIR=$B2/nbcache NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 brain/tests/brian2_first_divergence.py --conn $B2/flywire_export.npz --ref $B2/ref_sugar_times.npz --dt 0.1 --out $B2/div_default.json`, again with `--eps-v 0 --eps-g 0`, and again with `--eps-v 0 --eps-g 0 --float64` (NUMBA_CACHE_DIR keeps new compiled signatures out of brain/flybrain/__pycache__).
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps (and sharpens) the claim: first mismatch is at a neuron within ~0.01 mV of threshold and seed 0 becomes identical with eps=0 (or eps=0+float64) while seeds 1-2 stay identical -> the paper can say 'identical in all three seeds once the simulator's shortcut is turned off; with it, one near-threshold spike flips'. Forces a change: mismatch at a neuron > 0.05 mV from threshold, or divergence persists with eps=0+float64 -> a semantic difference; drop 'spike for spike' until found.

edge_cases.description: Brian2 vs kernel on the PAPER's model (known signs, eLN x0.25) with the drives the social claims rest on: cVA ORNs (export group in_orn_cva = ORN_DA1+DL3), food ORNs, head bristles, and sugar+bitter (inhibition); plus the published model's dense runaway regime (cVA, 6 % of neurons active, PPL1 ~106 Hz).
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Agreement has only been shown for one sparse regime (0.4 % active, feed-forward taste path, mostly the serial kernel path: the parallel pass starts at 3000*T active neurons). Dense recurrent regimes (antennal lobe, KC, PPL1 near max rate) are where refractory-boundary rules and the discard-during-refractory rule matter most; a mismatch there would not show up with sugar.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Existing flags only. `S=$TMPDIR/flycraft_brian2; cd .; FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 python3 brain/tests/export_for_brian2.py --dataset flywire --out $S/paper_export.npz; for D in in_orn_cva:100 in_orn_food:100 in_bristle:100 in_grn_sugar:100,in_grn_bitter:100; do n=$(echo $D | tr ':,' '__'); b2venv/bin/python brain/tests/brian2_reference.py --conn $S/paper_export.npz --drive $D --ms 1000 --seeds 3 --dt 0.1 --out $S/ref_paper_$n.npz && NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 brain/tests/compare_brian2.py --conn $S/paper_export.npz --ref $S/ref_paper_$n.npz --dt 0.1 > $S/cmp_paper_$n.txt; done; b2venv/bin/python brain/tests/brian2_reference.py --conn $S/flywire_export.npz --drive in_orn_cva:100 --ms 1000 --seeds 3 --dt 0.1 --out $S/ref_pub_cva.npz && python3 brain/tests/compare_brian2.py --conn $S/flywire_export.npz --ref $S/ref_pub_cva.npz --dt 0.1 > $S/cmp_pub_cva.txt`. Note: sugar+bitter is two PoissonGroups in Brian2 but one index-sorted draw loop in the kernel, so that drive can only agree statistically.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps: every output group printed by compare_brian2 (out_turn_L/R = DNa, out_PPL1, out_mb_kc, out_DNp13, out_feed, out_jump) within max(2 seed-SD, 10 %) of Brian2 and per-neuron r >= 0.99 for every drive (identical counts in some single-group seeds is a bonus). Forces change: any group off by > 3 SD or r < 0.95 in the odor/touch regime -> the paper can claim Brian2 agreement only for the taste pathway, and the mismatch must be traced before the odor/touch claims stand.

edge_cases.description: Repeat the Brian2 comparison at dt = 0.2 ms, the time step every result of the paper uses (the Brian2 check was only run at 0.1).
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Spike-for-spike agreement at 0.1 does not transfer automatically: at 0.2 the kick-to-spike latency, the delay (+1 step) and the refractory count are all different step counts, and Brian2's timestep() rounding conventions could disagree with the kernel's round(t_ref/dt) at the new step.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Existing flags. `b2venv/bin/python brain/tests/brian2_reference.py --conn $S/paper_export.npz --drive in_grn_sugar:100 --ms 1000 --seeds 3 --dt 0.2 --out $S/ref_paper_sugar_dt02.npz && python3 brain/tests/compare_brian2.py --conn $S/paper_export.npz --ref $S/ref_paper_sugar_dt02.npz --dt 0.2`; same with `--drive in_orn_cva:100` (out $S/ref_paper_cva_dt02.npz). Needs paper_export.npz from brian2-paper-model-odor-touch.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps: sugar identical in >= 2 of 3 seeds and cVA group rates within 2 SD / r >= 0.99 at dt 0.2. Forces change: systematic group-rate offset at 0.2 but not 0.1 -> the Brian2 equivalence holds only at Brian2's own step; either rerun the paper at 0.1 or state the offset.

edge_cases.description: Run the sugar comparison for 10 s (2 seeds) to measure how long spike-for-spike identity lasts and whether group rates still agree once trajectories part.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: One of three 1-s runs diverged, so identity is a short-horizon property (expected first flip within a few seconds); arena brains run for minutes. The paper's wording suggests identity is the norm.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Existing flags. `b2venv/bin/python brain/tests/brian2_reference.py --conn $TMPDIR/flycraft_brian2/flywire_export.npz --drive in_grn_sugar:100 --ms 10000 --seeds 2 --dt 0.1 --out $TMPDIR/flycraft_brian2/ref_sugar_10s.npz && python3 brain/tests/compare_brian2.py --conn $TMPDIR/flycraft_brian2/flywire_export.npz --ref $TMPDIR/flycraft_brian2/ref_sugar_10s.npz --dt 0.1`
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Expected and fine: counts no longer identical but every group rate within 2 SD and r >= 0.99 -> reword to 'identical until a near-threshold spike flips, typically within seconds; rates agree thereafter'. Forces change: group rates drift apart over 10 s (e.g. feed MNs > 10 % apart) -> a slow systematic difference hidden in 1 s tests.

edge_cases.description: Cross-check the 0.2 Hz background 'hum' (the substrate under every arena series since 19b) against Brian2: no sensory drive, noise on every neuron, 5 s, 2 seeds, paper's model.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The hum turns 28 k kicks/s into ~830 k spikes/s (noise_floor_*_10s.csv, ~30x amplification) and builds up over seconds: a near-critical regime where any numerical difference (snap, float32, refractory edge) is amplified. It has never been compared with Brian2.
edge_cases.how_to_run: NEW CODE: brian2_reference.py `--noise-hz` (float, default 0): if > 0 add `PoissonGroup(N, rates=noise_hz*Hz)` and `Synapses(pg, neu, on_pre='v += w_syn * f_poi', namespace=params)` connected one-to-one (`connect(j='i')`); compare_brian2.py `--noise-hz` passed to LIFParams(noise_hz=...). Run `b2venv/bin/python brain/tests/brian2_reference.py --conn $S/paper_export.npz --drive '' --noise-hz 0.2 --ms 5000 --seeds 2 --dt 0.2 --out $S/ref_hum.npz && python3 brain/tests/compare_brian2.py --conn $S/paper_export.npz --ref $S/ref_hum.npz --dt 0.2 --noise-hz 0.2`. Random streams differ (binomial+randint vs PoissonGroup), so statistical only.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps: total spikes within 10 % and out_turn_L/R, out_dn_all, out_feed within 2 seed-SD. Forces change: the kernel's hum amplification differs from Brian2's -> the arena substrate is a property of the simulator, not of Shiu's model; every hum-based arena number needs that caveat.

edge_cases.description: Restore the missing micro-network tests: tiny hand-built networks (no connectome) run through the kernel and Brian2 with deterministic inputs that hit the refractory and delay edges.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The refractory rule (arrivals and kicks discarded for 2.2 ms, arrival at step ref_until discarded, kick at ref_until allowed) is the change that moved feeding rates 1.8x; the docstring says it was 'established by direct test' but those scripts are not in the release, so the rule cannot be re-checked by a reader.
edge_cases.how_to_run: NEW CODE: brain/tests/micro_semantics.py (numpy/numba env) and brain/tests/micro_semantics_brian2.py (b2venv), sharing a JSON spec of scenarios: (1) one neuron kicked at fixed steps including spike+ref_steps-1, +ref_steps, +ref_steps+1; (2) chain A->B with a subthreshold weight, A's arrivals timed to land on B's refractory boundary; (3) an inhibitory synapse onto a kicked neuron; (4) two arrivals + a kick in the same step; (5) a 30-neuron random recurrent net with one sorted Poisson group, 1 s, seeds 0-4. Each at dt 0.1 and 0.2. Kernel side emulates a timed kick with set_drive([i],[1000/dt]) for one step (p = 1); Brian2 side uses SpikeGeneratorGroup -> on_pre 'v += 68.75*mV'. Both write (step, neuron) lists to JSON; a third call compares. Run: `python3 brain/tests/micro_semantics.py --out $S/micro_k.json && b2venv/bin/python brain/tests/micro_semantics_brian2.py --out $S/micro_b.json`.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps: scenarios 1-4 identical at both dt, scenario 5 identical in most seeds. Forces change: any deterministic scenario differs -> the kernel's refractory/delay semantics are not Brian2's, and the whole-brain agreement is partly luck of the tested regime.

edge_cases.description: Brian2 vs kernel on the male (MaleCNS, eLN x0.25), cVA ORNs at 100 Hz, 3 seeds, dt 0.1, with the kick fixed at 68.75 mV on both sides.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: No male comparison exists, and brian2_reference.py scales the kick by w_syn (0.275*0.542*250 = 37.3 mV for the male; 48 mV at gain 0.7) while the kernel keeps 68.75 mV (LIFParams.kick_mv 'independent of gain here'): a silent difference from Shiu's formulation that only matters for strongly inhibited sensory neurons, but it must be removed before comparing.
edge_cases.how_to_run: NEW CODE: brian2_reference.py `--kick-mv` (float, default None -> w_syn*f_poi); when given, on_pre 'v += kick' with kick = kick_mv*mV. Then `FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 python3 brain/tests/export_for_brian2.py --dataset malecns --out $S/male_export.npz && b2venv/bin/python brain/tests/brian2_reference.py --conn $S/male_export.npz --drive in_orn_cva:100 --ms 1000 --seeds 3 --dt 0.1 --kick-mv 68.75 --out $S/ref_male_cva.npz && python3 brain/tests/compare_brian2.py --conn $S/male_export.npz --ref $S/ref_male_cva.npz --dt 0.1`. Optionally repeat without --kick-mv to measure the kick-size effect. Run alone, gate >= 35 % free (25.6 M Brian2 synapses).
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps: out_DNp13, out_feed (contains MN9), out_jump within 2 SD, r >= 0.99. Forces change: disagreement -> 'reproduces Shiu et al.'s model' holds for the female only; with/without --kick-mv differing -> the fixed kick is a model choice to list under 'Mine' in Note 11.

edge_cases.description: Sweep dt 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.5 ms with 10 seeds on the headline readouts of the paper's female model, with two controls: a second dt 0.2 run on seeds 100-109 (the pure seed null, which also tests seed independence) and dt 0.1 with t_ref 2.0 ms and delay 2.4 ms (mimicking what dt 0.5 rounds to).
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The kernel integrates exactly between steps, but timing is quantised: refractory = round(2.2/dt) steps and effective synaptic latency = delay_steps+1 steps, i.e. 1.85 / 1.9 / 2.0 / 2.5 ms latency and 2.2 / 2.2 / 2.2 / 2.0 ms refractory at dt 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.5. Existing evidence already shows 10-20 % shifts at 0.5 and a possible +14 % MN9 shift between the Brian2-validated 0.1 and the production 0.2 (3 seeds, ~2.5 SE). 'Identical' is not what the files say.
edge_cases.how_to_run: NEW CODE: brain/tests/dt_sweep.py. Args: --dataset {flywire,malecns}; --seeds 10; --ms 1000; --hz 100; --configs comma list of dt:t_ref:delay:seed0 (default '0.05:2.2:1.8:0,0.1:2.2:1.8:0,0.2:2.2:1.8:0,0.2:2.2:1.8:100,0.5:2.2:1.8:0,0.1:2.0:2.4:0'); --inputs comma list of common.input_groups names (female default: none, sugar GRNs, touch (all head bristles), food odor, food + touch, cVA (Or67d/DA1), cVA + touch, sound (JO-B)); --out required, refuse any path under experiments/results. For each config: sim = LIF(cx.W, LIFParams(dt, t_ref, delay, w_syn=0.275*cx.w_syn_scale)); per input and seed s in seed0..seed0+seeds-1: sim.seed(s); sim.reset(); sim.set_drive(*common.drive_of(groups, hz)); counts = sim.run(ms); rates for every common.output_groups group (same formula as run_trials). Write long CSV and print mean +- SE per config with z vs dt 0.2 and the freeze indices (1 - DNa(X+touch)/DNa(X)). Run: `FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 brain/tests/dt_sweep.py --dataset flywire --seeds 10 --out $TMPDIR/flycraft_edge/dt_sweep_flywire.csv`.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps (reworded): dt 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2 agree within the seed null (|diff| < 2 SE, as large as dt 0.2 seeds 0-9 vs 100-109) on MN9, feed MNs, DNp13, DNa L/R and freeze indices, GF, PPL1, KC; the dt 0.5 shift is reproduced by dt 0.1 with t_ref 2.0 / delay 2.4 -> Note 1 becomes 'the same within seed noise at 0.05-0.2 ms; at 0.5 ms the refractory period rounds to 2.0 ms and strongly driven rates rise 10-20 %'. Forces change: dt 0.05/0.1 vs 0.2 differ beyond 2 SE on a headline number (e.g. MN9 77 vs 88) -> quote the size, or re-run the headline numbers at 0.1 ms (Brian2's own step); if the 0.1-with-rounded-params control does not reproduce dt 0.5, the dt effect is not just rounding and needs explaining.

claims.claim: Note 10 and long-draft Methods/Statistics: 'Offline results are seeded and reproduce to the digit on the same numba version and thread count. The thread count matters because the parallel pass delivers spikes in an order set by the number of threads ... when a dose row was re-run with 10 threads instead of 6, one of 39 seed-cells differed.' Note 10: 'Of the 123 result files, 54 came out identical to the digit, and the others differ in a few cells because the originals were made with other thread counts or older scripts: under my model by at most 3.3 Hz in any firing rate (4.5 Hz in one left-right steering difference) and by at most 0.004 in the learned weights.'
already_tested: 25-26 Sep full re-run at NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6: 54 of 123 files identical to the digit; differing files attributed to 3/5/10-thread originals or older scripts (compare_results_20260926.out); paper's-model social map 17/3780 cells differ (<= 1 Hz), paper's-model odor dose 13/6615 (one seed-cell, vinegar 25 Hz R seed 2, approach -0.5 -> 4.0), precontact near/far <= 3.25 Hz, conditioning weights <= 0.004
Dose-row seed-cells: 1/39 differ at 10 vs 6 threads (24 Sep), 0/39 with both at 6 (paper_numbers.py section Q check)
Brian2 core-check run twice (25 and 26 Sep) with identical kernel and Brian2 counts

Code reading (this audit): the only thread-dependent quantity is T = min(NUMBA_NUM_THREADS, 8) (lif.py l.311); T fixes neuron-to-chunk assignment (i % T) and hence the order of the spike loop, so only the float32 summation order into buf and the act_buf order change; no RNG draw or branch depends on T, integration is per-neuron and race-free, and the serial/parallel switch (par_min = 3000*T) computes the same thing

edge_cases.description: Zero-cost determinism test: when the live queue (logs/rerun_20260926_steps.tsv, 6 threads, numba 0.65.1) finishes, diff every rewritten file against the frozen 25-26 Sep re-run (also 6 threads, numba 0.65.1; lif.py unchanged since 14 Sep).
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: 'To the digit with the same thread count' has only been inferred from files whose original thread counts were not recorded; any hidden nondeterminism (script-level RNG, Python hash ordering in a script, rewiring RNG, uninitialised buffers) would show here.

Forces change: any simulation file differing -> the determinism sentence is false; find the source before the paper claims 'to the digit'.

edge_cases.description: Run the paper's female social map at NUMBA_NUM_THREADS = 1, 2, 6, 8, 10 and twice at 6, 5 seeds, plus the hum (0.2 Hz) at 6 and 8, all to a scratch folder, and compare cell by cell.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Tests three predictions from the code: 6 == 6 (determinism), 8 == 10 (T is capped at 8, so '10 threads' on 24 Sep was really 8 chunks), and T=1/2/6/8 differ only through chaotic amplification of float32 summation order; and measures how big that is relative to seed spread, especially in the near-critical hum regime.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Existing flags (social_probe.py is the only probe with --out). `S=$TMPDIR/flycraft_edge; mkdir -p $S; cd .; for T in 1 2 6 8 10; do NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=$T FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 experiments/social_probe.py --dataset flywire --seeds 5 --out $S/social_T$T.csv; done; NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 experiments/social_probe.py --dataset flywire --seeds 5 --out $S/social_T6b.csv; for T in 6 8; do NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=$T FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 experiments/social_probe.py --dataset flywire --seeds 3 --noise-hz 0.2 --out $S/social_hum_T$T.csv; done`. Analysis (pandas): merge on (input, seed), drop wall_s; per pair count differing cells, max |diff|, |diff| / per-input seed SD, total_spikes equality per seed (trajectory fingerprint), and whether any readout crosses the 2 Hz presence line.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps: T6 == T6b and T8 == T10 bit-identical; between-T differences no larger than seed-to-seed spread and no presence/absence call flips -> Methods should say 'NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 (the simulator uses min(threads, 8) chunks); another thread count acts like a fresh draw of the noise'. Forces change: 6 != 6b (nondeterminism) or 8 != 10 (something besides chunking depends on threads), or between-T differences exceed seed spread (then 3-seed means are thread-dependent and need more seeds).

edge_cases.description: The steering claims ride on 1-5 Hz differences; re-run the paper's odor dose with 10 seeds at two chunk counts (6 and 8) to see whether 'cVA on one antenna turns the female towards it by 0.6-2.3 Hz' survives.

notes:
1) Note 1's "results identical at 0.1-0.5 ms" is contradicted by the project's own files. logs/reproduce_core-check.out is the published model at 500 ms with 3 seeds. At dt 0.5 there, cVA->PPL1 goes 105.9 -> 116.4 Hz and KC goes 30.4 -> 36.2 (seed SD < 1), and sugar->feed goes 24.7 -> 28.8. test_lif.py still prints "AGREE" because its tolerance is 3*max(SD, 15 % of mean, 1 Hz), up to about 45 %. In the paper's-model sensitivity table, sugar->MN9 is 77.2 at dt 0.2, 87.8 at 0.1 and 86.1 at 0.5, and feed MNs are 24.1 / 26.7 / 28.9 (3 seeds). The cause is rounding: at dt 0.5 the refractory period becomes 4 steps (2.0 ms), and the effective synaptic latency (delay_steps+1) becomes 2.5 ms, against 1.9 ms at dt 0.1 and 2.0 ms at 0.2. The same wording appears in the lif.py docstring, the run_brain.py --dt help and the long draft.
2) The Brian2 agreement has only been shown for the published model: export_for_brian2 ran without FLYBRAIN_SIGNS/ELN. It was also only tested with sugar drive (0.4 % of neurons active, so mostly the serial kernel path), only at dt 0.1 (the paper uses 0.2), and only for 1 s. "A single neuron ... tips" understates the third seed: that run differs in 284 of 592 active neurons (0.75 % of spikes; 16 neurons active only in Brian2, 6 only in the kernel). The near-threshold cause was inferred, not shown. The likelier trigger is the rest-snapping shortcut (eps_v = 0.01 mV, about 1000x float32 resolution). The lif.py docstring cites "brain/tests/ micro-network scripts, 14 Sep 2026" as evidence for the refractory rule, but no such scripts exist in brain/tests.
3) Thread count. The effective parameter is T = min(NUMBA_NUM_THREADS, 8) (lif.py l.311), so 8, 10 or 12 threads give identical chunking; the "10 threads" run of 24 Sep was really T = 8. Thread count only changes the float32 summation order in spike delivery; chaotic dynamics then amplify it. The paper should name NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6, because a reader's default is their core count.
4) Silent modelling choice: the kick is fixed at 68.75 mV at every gain and in the male. brian2_reference.py (like Shiu's code) scales it with w_syn: 37.3 mV for the male and 48 mV at gain 0.7. This is harmless from rest, but it has to be fixed before any male or gain != 1 Brian2 comparison, and it belongs in Note 11's list of choices that are "mine".
5) Long runs. No run longer than 1 s without noise exists. The 10 s hum files show a slow build-up (DNa 7/7 -> 18/20 Hz at 0.2 Hz noise). MN9, a single neuron, is bimodal under the hum: 2 / 24 / 85 Hz across seeds in 1 s, 79 Hz at 10 s, and 69 Hz with cVA + hum at 10 s against 1.3 Hz at 1 s. That looks like a latch. Around 830 k spikes/s come out of 28 k kicks/s, which is near-critical.
6) Note 9 says "cVA on one antenna turns the female towards it by 0.6-2.3 Hz". With paper_numbers.py's steer formula the frozen file gives 1.67 / 0.58 / -0.17 / 2.33 Hz at 50 / 75 / 100 / 150 Hz. The 100 Hz cell (-0.17 +- 2.77) is left out of the range, and per-seed values run from -2.75 to +4.0 with 3 seeds. One seed-cell of the same file moved 4.5 Hz between thread counts, so the effect is within seed and thread noise.
7) Arena seeds. run_pair.sh passes the same extra args to both brains, and encounter_trials.sh adds only --noise-hz. So every arena brain (both flies, every trial) runs with LIF and motor RNG seed 0. The paired ff hum logs I checked already differ at tick 1, so the two brains are not identical copies, but trials are not seed-independent replicates. This matters for statistics that treat fly-logs as independent (the 24/33 sign test).
8) Latent code issues, none triggered by current calls. LIF.run rounds ms/dt with Python's banker's rounding while callers divide counts by the requested ms, so an ms value that is not a multiple of dt gives biased rates. LIF.reset() does not clear the drive. LIF.seed() seeds numba's process-global RNG.
9) Cost and safety. Measured peaks (logs/guarded_peaks.tsv): core-check including the Brian2 female run 1,528 MB; odor-code including the male 1,382 MB. Every edge case here except Brian2-male (~3.5 GB, estimated) stays under 2 GB. Only social_probe.py and compare_results.py take --out; every other probe writes into experiments/results. So run the edge cases only after the live queue (logs/rerun_20260926_steps.tsv, 6 threads) finishes, one at a time. Use experiments/run_guarded.sh with a step file in scratch and MEMLOG/PEAKS/OUTDIR/DONE pointed at scratch, or the runner will write into logs/. The export and ref_sugar.npz of the published model are already in $TMPDIR/flycraft_brian2. The best order is same-threads-rerun-diff (free, 1 min), then brian2-first-divergence, dt-sweep-female, long-run-drift and thread-sweep (~1.5 h in total). All four notes claims 1-3 should be reworded whatever the outcome ("identical" for dt, "a single neuron" for Brian2, "thread count" for T).

notes:
TEXT THAT DISAGREES WITH THE RESULT FILES OR OVERSTATES THEM (frozen copy release/pre_rerun_20260926/results):
1. Freeze: main text says 'survives every one of my alternatives but one'. It was tested only on contact_stop's 8 table conditions (6 sign x eLN + 2 Zenodo), plus gains. sensitivity.py has no food+touch -> DNa pair, so stimulus 50/150 Hz, dt 0.1/0.5, legacy numerics and the Shiu-table >= 5 condition were never run. The reversal is shown only for the Zenodo table at >= 5 (top_nt signs + known override). Zenodo at min1 freezes (0.71), so within Zenodo the threshold matters, but 'remove the connections made of fewer than five synapses ... touch excites the steering neurons' is untested on the paper's own table.
2. Shuffle: 'Scramble the wiring and every one of these reflexes disappears' / Note 4 'Every readout 0-2 Hz in a rewired brain'. wind -> aBN1, bitter suppression and male ppk -> wing/song MNs were never recorded in any rewired brain (shuffle_control keep_in / keep_out lack them). The global null silences every input (DN-all <= 0.2 Hz, even for 1,417 bristles at 100 Hz), so it cannot tell specific from non-specific wiring. The only stricter null (block, published lobe) keeps JO-A -> GF at 4.4-7.5 Hz vs 10-11 intact, touch -> DNp13 at 9-14, and raises touch -> MDN to 23-40 and touch -> DNa to 33-67. RESEARCH_NOTES 14v says block 'sound -> giant fiber 0-0.6 Hz': that is JO-B, not the JO-A the paper quotes. The block null was never run on the paper's model or the male. Minor: RESEARCH_NOTES 22 says the re-run block moved 91.6-91.7 %; that is an intermediate progress line in logs/reproduce_shuffle.out (1.98 swaps/edge), and the final is 94.3 %.
3. wind -> aBN1 and bitter suppression have no gain, sensitivity or shuffle test at all (benchmark only, gain 1.0). The paper's own rule says a behaviour needs all three.
4. Male backing: main text 'When his legs touch a female ... fails the gentlest version of my first test'. Leg-taste (ppk23/25) -> MDN is 0 / 26.8 / 1.8 Hz at gains 0.7 / 1.0 / 1.4 (all 5 seeds <= 2.9 at 1.4), so it fails 0.7 AND 1.4. Only head-bristle -> MDN fails 0.7 alone, and that one is 0.0 Hz at a 50 Hz stimulus. Bristle -> MDN also depends on the odour context (Or47b + touch 2.8, food + touch 4.0, alone 10.7, cVA + touch 21.6, CO2 + touch 46.8 Hz). The arena male smells the female's Or47b, so arena backing is probably carried by ppk.
5. Male cVA: 'no other smell at all' / Note 4 'every other odour 0'. This holds for DNp13 in both lobes, but for MN9 only under eLN x0.25. Under the published lobe every odour drives MN9 at 19-22 Hz (cVA 27; social_probe_malecns_all_min1_noise0.csv), yet Note 3 says every smell result is reported both ways. Other odours are also 1.3-2.8 Hz on MN9 in the paper's model, not 0. RESEARCH_NOTES 18k 'every other odor -> DNp13 is 0.0 in every condition' is not backed by sensitivity_malecns (only cVA and food+touch pairs exist there).
6. Unreported laterality: odor_dose_malecns gives left-only cVA -> DNp13 0-4.3 Hz and MN9 0.5-2.0 (25-100 Hz) against right-only up to 27.7 / 36.8. MaleCNS labels DA1 ORNs 105 right / 51 left / 48 'na', so it is at least partly an annotation-count effect.
7. Female 'head touch' offline means all 1,417 BM_ neurons at 100 Hz, and in the body all of them at 200 Hz (binary, bilateral, senses.py R_BURST). Antennal bristles alone (41 neurons) give DNp13 2.0 Hz. The closing experimental prediction has never been simulated with a partial or one-sided touch.
8. JO-A -> GF is absent from sensitivity.py. JO-B, the tested sound input, fails at 50 Hz (0.3) and >= 5 synapses (0.8). Odours reach GF at 3-5 Hz at gain 1.0, half of JO-A's 11.
9. 'Wing motor neurons 10-22 Hz' is the song-MNs column. The same neurons get 14 Hz from wind, 10 from head touch and 12.6 from cVA, so this is a response, not a specific one.
10. MN9 R (720575940645521262) is not in v783, so benchmark 'MN9 both' = MN9 L (NaN column).

edge_cases.description: NEW experiments/decider_drive.py. Args: --dataset, --gain (1.0), --hz (100), --ms (1000), --seeds (3), --noise-hz (0), --vstep-ms (1.0), --inputs (default: every input_groups entry plus two unions: 'ALL social' = ORN_DA1/DL3/VA1v/VA1d/DC3 + JO-A + JO-B + BM_* [+ ppk23/25 in the male] and 'ALL sensory' = union of every input group), --out. Per (input, seed): run the sim in vstep chunks (sim.run(1.0) repeatedly, summing counts), sample sim.v for the reported neurons after each chunk. Reported neurons: female pC1a, pC1b, pC1c, pC1d, pC1e, aIPg (hemibrain ^aIPg), vpoEN, DNp37, oviDN*, aSP-g; controls DNp13, DNa01/02, MN9 (SHIU_MN9), DNp01, MDN. Per neuron: rate; E = sum over W_ij>0 of W_ij*r_i and I = sum over W_ij<0 of |W_ij|*r_i (syn*Hz, from the per-neuron rate vector and the precomputed column slice W[:, targets]); mean-field depolarisation = 0.275*w_syn_scale*gain*0.005*(E-I) mV (threshold gap 7 mV, i.e. 5,091 syn*Hz at gain 1 in the female); v_mean and v_max above rest; fraction of time within 1 mV of threshold; n active presynaptic partners / n partners; top-3 presynaptic types by W_ij*r_i. Outputs decider_drive_<dataset>_<variant>_g<gain>_hz<hz>.csv and a _groups.csv with max per-neuron rate per group. Run at (gain 1.0, 100 Hz) and (gain 1.4, 300 Hz).
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Tests the sentence 'the paths carry nothing' directly. If deciders receive large excitation cancelled by inhibition (E ~ I), the miss is an inhibitory gate (the sign rule / E-I balance of Clowney et al. 2015), not an empty path. If v_max sits within 1-2 mV of threshold, the silence is fragile.
edge_cases.how_to_run: New script as specified; then: cd . && PATH=$HOME/.pyenv/shims:$PATH NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=3 FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 python3 experiments/decider_drive.py --dataset flywire --gain 1.0 --hz 100 --seeds 3 --out experiments/results_edge/ && (same with --gain 1.4 --hz 300)
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps (with an explanation): for every input E is near 0 (presynaptic partners silent) and v_max < ~3 mV above rest -> 'nothing arrives' is literal. Forces a change: (i) E >= threshold drive but cancelled by I -> text must say inhibition shuts the path; (ii) any decider with v_max within 1 mV of threshold at gain <= 1.4 -> 'silent but at the edge of firing'.

edge_cases.description: NEW experiments/decider_paths.py (no simulation; both sexes, paper's variant via env). Sources: every single sensory class of input_groups (DA1, DL3, VA1v, VA1d, DC3, food, CO2, aversive, JO-A, JO-B, JO-CE, BM all/Ant/InOm, sugar, bitter; male + ppk23, ppk25, ppk23/25) plus positive-control sources SAG (female) and P1/pC1 (male). Targets: each decider type separately (female pC1a..e, aIPg, vpoEN, DNp37, oviDN, aSP-g; male every pC1_* subtype, aIPg, pIP10, vpoEN, mAL) and reflex targets that DO respond (DNp13, DNa01/02, MN9, DNp01, MDN). Metrics per (source, target, graph in {all edges, W>0 only, |W|>=5}): (a) min hop count by frontier propagation (boolean sparse matvec, up to 8 hops) and number of target neurons reached at that hop; (b) propagated weight: Wn = W / column sum of |W| (signed fraction of each neuron's input synapses), x0 = 1 on sources, x_k = clip(x_{k-1} @ Wn, 0, 1), report mean over target of x_k for k = 1..8, signed-rectified and excitatory-only (Wn+); (c) strongest excitatory path by Dijkstra on cost -log(Wn+) from a virtual super-source, with its cell-type chain and weakest link; (d) per decider neuron: total input synapses, exc/inh split, top-10 presynaptic types with sign and their hop distance from each source. Outputs decider_paths_<dataset>_<variant>.csv, decider_bestpath_*.csv, decider_inputs_*.csv.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: If a silent pair (e.g. cVA -> pC1a or JO-A -> vpoEN, the real-fly pathways of Zhou et al. 2014 / Wang et al. 2021) scores as short and as heavy as a responding reflex (cVA -> DNa, touch -> DNp13), the silence is dynamic and the paper's explanation ('no path') is wrong; if it scores far below, the paper gains the WHY.

Forces a change: any silent pair within the range of responding pairs -> rewrite 'the paths carry nothing' as 'the paths exist but are held shut' and point at signs/inhibition.

notes:
TEXT VS RESULT FILES (draft 5 dropped qualifiers the long draft still had):
1. 'pC1a-e, aIPg, vpoDN and oviDN ... in all 14 conditions' is not what was run. sensitivity.py PAIRS contain only cVA -> pC1d/e and cVA -> aIPg (0.0 in all 14). pC1a, pC1b/c, vpoDN and oviDN, and every non-cVA input, were never run under the 14 conditions. 'At every gain up to 1.4' is also only partly tested: gain_sweep.py does not record pC1b/c or oviDN, and its only combinations are cVA+touch and food+touch. The 'every input and combination' part holds only for the gain-1.0 innate map (26 inputs + none, 5 seeds, all six groups 0.0).
2. 'Male P1 stays at or below 0.6 Hz' holds only at gain <= 1.0 and in 12 of 13 conditions: 0.65 with >=5 synapses and 2.5 under the first-version numerics. At gain 1.4 P1 is 1.6-2.3 Hz and male aIPg is 1.4-1.9 Hz. paper_numbers.md computes 2.3 / 1.9 itself. P1 is a mean over ~148-156 neurons in ~45 pC1_* subtypes, and per-neuron rates were never looked at.
3. 'pIP10 answers cVA only, at 2-3.5 Hz' is the gain-1.0 map (max 3.7, cVA + song). It is 7.5-8 Hz at gain 1.4 and 1.1-6.9 Hz across the 13 conditions.
4. 'No sign rule steers towards food' contradicts the existing 3-seed files:
   - Zenodo table: vinegar at 150 Hz +6.5 +/- 1.0 Hz (all three seeds positive), sweet at 150 Hz +3.6 +/- 1.8, CO2 at 100 Hz +6.4.
   - Shiu signs: food +1.2 to +2.7 Hz at all five doses, ester at 150 Hz +3.8.
   The long draft said 'up to +6.5 Hz at 150 Hz'; draft 5 dropped it. '16-29 Hz left turn whatever the odour' holds for the food-type odours (15.8-29.2); for CO2 and aversive the bias is 0 at 25 Hz. That file is Shiu signs with eLN x0.25, not the published lobe.
5. The long draft lists 'contact pheromones' among the female's inputs. FlyWire has no receptor_type column and no ppk23/25 neurons (it is brain only), so the female was never given contact pheromone or any leg input. input_groups silently drops those groups.
6. Calling gain 2.0 'runaway' is weak for sound. In the paper's female model, JO-A/JO-B at gain 2.0 wake pC1d/e to 3.8-4.1 Hz with only 4 % of neurons active (touch 8 %). The 11-12 % runaway figure comes from the published lobe (14g).
7. The clean box is not 'nothing to smell': each female smells the other's Or47b at 0.10-0.12 and CO2 at 0.003 (19a). The stillness depends on staying below the Or47b x CO2 ignition window. The replication's clean-ff logs have only 77 +/- 72 s of brain time.
8. The model shows untested signs of self-sustained, bistable activity:
   - The hum's DNa response grows from 3 to 17 Hz between 1 s and 10 s at 0.1 Hz, then saturates.
   - The cVA dose row jumps from 0 to 15 Hz between 0.06 and 0.14.
   - The Or47b + CO2 response is all-or-none by seed.
   The persistence edge case targets this.

claims.claim: Note 3: 'Published model: one glomerulus driven at 100 Hz makes 81% of the 685 projection neurons and 65% of the 5,177 Kenyon cells fire, the same cells for every odour (Jaccard overlap 0.99).'
already_tested: 9 single glomeruli (DM2, DL5, DA1, VA1v, DM1, VM2, V, DC3, DA2) plus the 5-glomerulus food blend, 2 seeds, 500 ms, 100 Hz: PN active 80-82%, KC active 65-66% for every odour, between-odour Jaccard 0.976-0.992 (verified from the frozen CSV)

published lobe in the 14-condition sensitivity table (food -> KC 33 Hz)

claims.claim: Note 3: 'After [known signs + eLN x0.25] a single odour drives 18% of glomeruli and 0-5% of Kenyon cells, as in real flies (Honegger 2011), with overlaps of 0.63 within and 0.08 between odours.'
already_tested: 2 seeds, 10 odours, 100 Hz, 500 ms; eLN x0.1 / x0.5 / x1 comparison
library odours at 25-150 Hz in odor_dose (bilateral KC active 1.2-7.2%)
sensitivity table at 50 and 150 Hz (KC mean rate only, no glomerular spread or overlap)
male at eLN x0.25 (1 seed, so no within-odour overlap)

edge_cases.description: Recompute the within/between KC overlaps with Jaccard(empty, empty) = NaN rather than 0, and report them only over odours that produce a KC code (>= 0.5% of KCs). Design-phase recomputation from the frozen overlap CSV: 3 of 10 odours (DA2, VA1v, VM2) have no or almost no KC code; over the 7 that do, overlap is 0.76 within and 0.16 between (largest pair DA1-DC3 0.34). The paper's 0.63 / 0.08 is pulled down by zeros from empty sets.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: odor_code.py computes (A&B).sum()/max((A|B).sum(),1), so two empty codes score 0. That deflates both the 'within' and the 'between' number, and the quoted separation partly measures odours that never reach the memory centre.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Patch odor_code.py overlap loop: jac.append(np.nan if (A|B).sum()==0 else (A&B).sum()/(A|B).sum()) and use np.nanmean; add a 'live' flag per odour (mean kc_active >= 0.005). Then re-run into a separate dir: OUT=release/edge_20260927 SCRIPT=experiments/odor_code.py python3 -c "$REDIR" --dataset flywire --seeds 3 --variants shiu,known,known+eln0.5,known+eln0.25,known+eln0.1. Update the paper_numbers.py section I check to the live-only numbers.

Either way the paper's numbers must change to the live-only values, and it must say that 3 of 10 test odours reach no Kenyon cells, so '0-5%' includes zeros.

edge_cases.description: Drive every one of the 53 ORN glomeruli alone, plus each of the 7 ODOR_LIBRARY classes the arena uses (ester, vinegar, floral, green, sweet, aversive, food). Get the distribution of glomerular spread and KC recruitment, and the KC overlap between library classes that share glomeruli by design (ester, sweet, vinegar and food share DM1, DM2, DM4, VA2, VM2).
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: '18% of glomeruli' is the mean of a bimodal set: 6 single glomeruli spread to 23-28%, 3 stay at 2-3%, and the blend reaches 20%. The 9 test glomeruli may not be representative. If most single glomeruli recruit no KCs, 'as in real flies' fails. And the library classes the learning and arena results use were never checked for overlap.

Odours: each ORN_<glom> type (select cell_type ^ORN_<glom>$), plus SensoryEncoder(cx).odor(cls, r_max=hz) bilaterally for each ODOR_LIBRARY class. Per odour x seed, write: glomeruli_over_10hz computed over the 53 glomeruli that have ORNs (drop the 'multi', 'M', 'MZ', 'Z' PN bins that odor_code.py counts in its 59), cognate PN Hz, KC active fraction, per-glomerulus PN rate vector. Save KC active sets to a .npz. Overlap CSV: KC Jaccard (NaN for empty/empty) and cosine similarity of PN vectors. Outputs go to $OUT/odor_code_all_<dataset>.csv, _overlap.csv and _kcsets.npz. Run: FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 python3 experiments/odor_code_all.py --dataset flywire --variants known+eln0.25 --hz 100 150 --seeds 3 --odors both

If most single glomeruli give 0% KCs, or the library classes overlap > 0.5, Note 3 must say that only some odours reach the memory centre and give the real spread distribution.

conditioning at x0.1 (LI 0.62) and x0.25 (0.54)

If the transition is sharp and odour-dependent (some odours ignite, others not, at the same scale), say so.

edge_cases.description: Find which 'excitatory' local neurons cause the runaway. The 150 scaled neurons are not all cholinergic. RESEARCH_NOTES 16a lists 166 LNs made excitatory by the majority vote: 72 predicted ACh, 40 5-HT, 12 DA, and 40 GABA/Glu-predicted neurons whose vote still came out positive. 16 flip under known signs. Scale or silence each subset separately.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Note 3 calls them '150 cholinergic local neurons', and the main text justifies the cut with Yaksi & Wilson's electrical coupling of cholinergic eLNs. If the runaway is carried by the serotonin/dopamine-predicted or GABA/Glu-predicted '+' neurons, the justification describes the wrong cells, and the principled fix is a sign/transmitter correction rather than a x0.25 dial.
edge_cases.how_to_run: New script experiments/eln_subset.py. Load connectome.load(dataset='flywire', signs='known', eln_scale=1.0), row_sign = sign(W.sum(1)), eLN = select(cell_class='^ALLN$') with row_sign>0. Split by the top_nt column: ach / mod (serotonin|dopamine|octopamine) / gg (gaba|glutamate), and print the counts. Variants, each built as cx.W = diags(scale) @ W exactly as apply_model_options does: (a) all eLN x0.25 (must reproduce odor_code known+eln0.25); (b) ACh-only x0.25, others x1; (c) non-ACh x0.25 only; (d) mod x0 (no fast output), ACh x1; (e) mod x0 + ACh x0.25; (f) gg-predicted '+' LNs flipped to -1, ACh x1. For each, run the odor_code protocol (the same 10 odours, 100 Hz, 500 ms, 3 seeds) and write $OUT/eln_subset_flywire.csv plus _overlap.csv (live-only Jaccard).
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Supports the stated biology if (b) alone brings glomerular spread <= 35% and live between-Jaccard <= 0.25. If (b) still runs away (> 60% glomeruli) while (c), (d) or (f) stop it, reword Note 3 and the main text: the culprits are local neurons the sign rule mislabels as excitatory, not the weak cholinergic eLN pull. In every case, correct '150 cholinergic' to '150 local neurons the sign rule makes excitatory, about half predicted cholinergic'.

notes:
Text that disagrees with the result files (frozen copy release/pre_rerun_20260926/results):
(1) Note 9: 'cVA on one antenna turns her towards it by 0.6-2.3 Hz' (RESEARCH_NOTES 22b says 'at 50-150 Hz'). The file gives +1.67 / +0.58 / -0.17 / +2.33 Hz at 50 / 75 / 100 / 150 Hz and 0 at 25 Hz. No rate is significant at n = 3 (t <= 1.94), and CO2 steers by similar amounts. paper_numbers.py never checks this range.
(2) Note 3 overlaps '0.63 within / 0.08 between'. These are deflated because odor_code.py scores Jaccard(empty, empty) = 0. DA2, VA1v and VM2 give no KC code (0-0.1% of KCs). Over the 7 odours that have a code, overlap is 0.76 within and 0.16 between (largest pair DA1-DC3 0.34). At eLN x0.1 only 2 of 10 odours reach KCs at all, so its '0.51 / 0.01' mostly measures silence.
(3) '18% of glomeruli' is the mean of a bimodal set: 6 single glomeruli spread to 23-28%, 3 stay at 2-3%, the blend reaches 20%. The 59-bin denominator also includes non-glomerular PN bins ('multi', 'M', 'MZ', 'Z') and VP glomeruli without ORNs.
(4) '150 cholinergic local neurons' is inaccurate. RESEARCH_NOTES 16a: 166 AL LNs are excitatory by majority vote (72 predicted ACh, 40 5-HT, 12 DA, 40 GABA/Glu with a positive vote); 16 flip under known signs, leaving 150. top_nt over all 429 ALLNs in the annotation TSV: Glu 148, GABA 147, ACh 80, 5-HT 40, DA 12, OA 2. The long draft's appendix repeats 'cholinergic'.
(5) 'Nothing that does not involve smell depends on the change' holds at gains 0.7 and 1.0 for the female, but fails at 1.4, inside the paper's own robustness window, in the existing gain sweeps. Published-lobe touch ignites the lobe in 3 of 3 seeds: KC 49 Hz, DNp13 19 vs 42, DNa L 27.5 vs 2, PPL1 133 vs 0. Sugar -> MN9 is 64+-30 vs 94. At gain 1.0, female sugar ignites the published lobe in 1 of 5 social-map seeds, and male sugar gives PPL1 56+-40 vs 12 and song MNs 4.9 vs 0. Male touch/ppk rows match under both lobes.
(6) Note 5's 'No sign rule steers towards food' is contradicted by the steering component under Shiu signs x0.25: +1.2 to +2.7 Hz towards food, t up to 4.6, hidden by a 15-25 Hz left bias. 'Food turns her away' holds only for known signs on the Shiu table; the Zenodo table gives -1.3 to +1.7.
(7) At gain 0.7 odours do not drive the DNa at all (gain sweep: cVA 0/0, food 0.2/0). Any chemotaxis claim therefore fails the 0.7 / 1.0 / 1.4 presence rule unless the paper says steering needs gain >= 1.0.
(8) The long draft contradicts itself: the answer table says smells are told apart 'only with the dial at <= 0.5', while the text says 0.25 is 'the largest value'. No criterion for 'keeps smells apart' was ever written down, and the grid is only 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.

The pooled lean (Note 9), analysed in this design phase with read-only scripts on the logs and the frozen encounter_trials.csv ((scratch, not kept) and lean2.py):
- The 24/9 split reproduces, and the sign convention is right.
- Against a within-pre-contact time-shift null (which keeps each log's turning bias and partner-side distribution), P = 0.15 for the count and 0.29 for the mean index. A whole-log shift gives P = 0.05.
- 29 of 35 female logs turn right on average before contact.
- The existing 10-seed near-level precontact file shows a bilateral partner odour driving DNa R > L (turn -0.11 to -0.15) for both male and female partners.
- The lean comes from the faint-smell and hum series, not the clean boxes.
The likely story is an odour-evoked rightward turning bias plus the geometry of approaching a stationary male, not steering. The clause 'about the size of the pull his pheromone has' compares a unilateral bench number to a bilateral arena situation.

- odor_code.py writes the fixed names odor_code_<dataset>.csv and _overlap.csv.

It works because the scripts do 'from common import RES' after common is already imported. The alternative is a 2-line --tag / --suffix flag like noise_floor.py's --suffix.
- social_probe.py has --out.
- gain_sweep.py and odor_dose.py with --gain != 1 or new FLYBRAIN_ELN values write new names.

- Female sims run about 0.7 s of wall time per brain-second.
- Every priority-1 and priority-2 edge case above is female-only except nonsmell-both-lobes-gain, which includes the male at gain 1.4 (budget about 4 GB). Together they come to about 2.5 h, each at <= 2 GB except that one.

- The male at eLN x0.25 gives <= 0.2% KCs for 8 of 10 odours from a single seed, so '0-5% as in real flies' is weaker in the male.

If pC1a < 2 Hz at 0.7, Note 6 and the main text must say the virgin state works only at gain >= 1.0 (a gain window, which the innate reflexes do not have). edge_cases.description: SAG (and every other female state) at 10, 20, 30, 60 and 100 Hz on the paper's model, 10 seeds each. The 30 Hz run doubles as a held-out-seed and reproducibility check.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The planned 10/30/100 Hz row (RESEARCH_NOTES 15, to-do 2) was never run on the paper's model. The only 100 Hz file is the published lobe at 3 seeds. A threshold (pC1a = 0 at 10-20 Hz) would make the virgin result depend on an arbitrary drive rate. Saturation or a nonlinear jump would change the 'scales with SAG' reading.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Same wrapper W as female-state-gain-window: for hz in 10 20 30 60 100; do mkdir -p experiments/results_edge/state_dose && FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore python3 -c "$W" experiments/results_edge/state_dose --dataset flywire --seeds 10 --state-hz $hz; done   (writes state_probe_flywire_shiu_min1+known+eln0.25_state{10,20,30,60,100}.csv in results_edge/state_dose). Analysis: pC1a / SAG-readout ratio per rate; lowest rate with pC1a > 1 Hz.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps the claim if pC1a, pC1b/c and vpoEN/DN rise monotonically from 10 Hz with no threshold, and the ratio stays within about 0.6-0.8. Report the curve in Note 6. If pC1a is about 0 at 10-20 Hz, the text must name a threshold. If the 30 Hz means at seeds 5-9 differ from seeds 0-4 by more than 2 s.e.m., the 21 / 19 / 5.7 numbers should be re-quoted from 10 seeds.

edge_cases.description: Specificity null. For SAG (2 neurons), draw 20 random 2-neuron sets from the same super_class (ascending), each member matched to a SAG neuron on total |W| output synapses within +/-25%. Drive them at 30 Hz with input none or touch, 3 seeds, and read pC1a-e, vpoEN/DN, recruited spikes. Also answers whether 'any 2 tonic neurons wake pC1'.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: If random ascending neurons of similar output strength also wake pC1 or vpoDN, the virgin result is a drive-strength artefact and not the SAG -> pC1 wiring.
edge_cases.how_to_run: NEW SCRIPT experiments/state_null.py. Args: --dataset; --mode matched|global|block; --groups (';' state names, default 'virgin (SAG tonic);courting male (P1/pC1 tonic);hungry (NPF tonic);fed (IPC tonic)', absent groups skipped); --draws 20; --shuffles 2; --swaps-per-edge 3; --state-hz 30; --inputs 'none;touch (all head bristles);sugar GRNs'; --seeds 3; --ms 1000; --outdir experiments/results_edge. matched: candidate pool = neurons with the group's majority super_class, excluding the group and every readout set, where each candidate's row sum of |cx.W| is within +/-25% of the member it replaces (widen to +/-50% if the pool has < 10); rng = np.random.default_rng(1000+draw); store the drawn root_ids as a ';' string. global/block: Wn = shuffle_control.rewire(cx.W, np.random.default_rng(100+s), swaps_per_edge, block) (the same rng seeds as Fig 6, so these are the already-reported shuffled brains), then LIF(Wn, LIFParams(w_syn=0.275*cx.w_syn_scale)), driving the labelled state neurons (indices unchanged); include intact rows. Output <outdir>/state_null_<dataset>_<variant>_<mode>.csv with columns mode, draw_or_shuffle, group, root_ids, input, seed, n_driven, total_spikes, recruited_spikes and the state_probe readouts. Run: FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 experiments/state_null.py --dataset flywire --mode matched --draws 20 --seeds 3
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps and strengthens the claim if pC1a, pC1b/c and vpoEN/DN are <= 1 Hz in >= 19 of 20 random draws (SAG's 21 Hz far outside the null). Fails if the median draw exceeds 5 Hz on pC1a. The paper would then have to say the effect is 'any tonic ascending input', not SAG.

edge_cases.description: Drive the same 2 SAG neurons (and NPF / IPC) at 30 Hz in 2 globally rewired female brains (the Fig 6 shuffles, rng 100 and 101), inputs none, touch and sugar, 3 seeds. Also read recruited spikes.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The orchestrator asked whether a shuffled brain also wakes pC1 under SAG drive. With degree-preserving rewiring SAG keeps its out-degree and weights, so any pC1a response in the shuffle means the result comes from SAG's output mass and not from its targets. The outcome is almost certainly pC1a about 0 (2 target neurons among 139k), so this mainly strengthens a claim reviewers will poke. The matched null above is the stronger test.
edge_cases.how_to_run: experiments/state_null.py (spec in state-matched-random-null): FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 experiments/state_null.py --dataset flywire --mode global --shuffles 2 --groups 'virgin (SAG tonic);hungry (NPF tonic);fed (IPC tonic)' --seeds 3. Optionally --mode block --shuffles 1.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Passes if SAG gives pC1a, pC1b/c and vpoEN/DN <= 1 Hz in every shuffle while the intact rows reproduce 21 / 19 / 5.7. Report the recruited-spike count too: it shows whether SAG's reach survives rewiring. Any pC1a above 5 Hz in a shuffle forces a rewrite of 'produced by the wiring plus one state'.

edge_cases.description: State grid under the connection threshold that reversed the freeze (>= 5 synapses per connection), paper's model, 5 seeds, 30 Hz.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The freeze result lives on weak connections. If the SAG -> pC1 -> vpoDN relay also needs sub-5-synapse connections, the state arm fails the same sensitivity condition, and the paper should say so.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Same wrapper W (FLYBRAIN_MIN_SYN is read by connectome.load; the variant becomes shiu_min5+known+eln0.25; the cache data/connectome_783_shiu_min5.npz exists): mkdir -p experiments/results_edge/state_min5 && FLYBRAIN_MIN_SYN=5 FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore python3 -c "$W" experiments/results_edge/state_min5 --dataset flywire --seeds 5
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Stands if SAG alone gives pC1a >= 5 Hz and vpoEN/DN > 1 Hz. If the response vanishes, Note 6 must say the virgin state rides on weak connections, as the freeze does.

claims.claim: Note 6: 'P1 -> pIP10 50, TN1 8 and the song motor neurons 28 Hz' (male, 148 pC1_/P1_ neurons at 30 Hz). Main text: 'Keep a male's courtship neurons firing and his brain sends its song command to the wing, with nobody there to sing to.'
already_tested: Both lobes identical to the digit for P1 alone (19e-m); re-run identical
Without a state: pIP10 <= 3.4 Hz for every input (cVA 2.5); gain sweep up to 1.4 and 13 male sensitivity conditions keep P1 <= 0.6 and pIP10 cVA-only 2-3.5 Hz
Arena: P1 / pIP10 at the substrate floor without a state (19b). Never run with P1 tonic in the arena
Not tested: gain, dose (no male 100 Hz file at all), shuffle, a random-drive null, subsets of the 148-neuron cluster

edge_cases.description: Full male state grid (8 states x 12 inputs, 5 seeds, 30 Hz) at gain 0.7 and 1.4, paper's model.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The male's innate reflexes are the gain-fragile ones (touch -> MDN only at 1.0; cVA -> DNp13 7.8 / 30 / 26). P1 -> pIP10 converges 148 inputs and is likely robust, but TN1 (8 Hz) and the VNC song MNs are further downstream and may drop out at 0.7.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Wrapper W (see female-state-gain-window): for g in 0.7 1.4; do mkdir -p experiments/results_edge/state_gain$g && FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore python3 -c "$W" experiments/results_edge/state_gain$g --dataset malecns --seeds 5 --gain $g; done. Run only when swap use is below about 3 GB and no other male job is running.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Stands with 'at gains 0.7-1.4' if P1 alone gives pIP10 >= 20 Hz and TN1 > 2 Hz at both gains, with no-state pIP10 still <= 4 Hz. If TN1 or song MNs vanish at 0.7, the text keeps 'song command' (pIP10) and drops 'to the wing'.

edge_cases.description: Drive 20 random sets of 148 central cholinergic neurons, each member matched on |W| output synapses to a P1 member (+/-25%), at 30 Hz, input none, 3 seeds. Read pIP10, TN1, song MNs, wing MNs and recruited spikes. Also the hunger groups matched by size.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: 148 neurons at 30 Hz is a large drive: P1 alone makes about 23k spikes/s, of which about 18.5k are recruited. If any 148 well-connected central neurons also reach pIP10 at tens of Hz, 'P1 switches on song' becomes 'a lot of central drive reaches the song command'.
edge_cases.how_to_run: experiments/state_null.py (spec in claim 1, state-matched-random-null): FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 experiments/state_null.py --dataset malecns --mode matched --draws 20 --groups 'courting male (P1/pC1 tonic);hungry (NPF tonic);fed (IPC tonic)' --inputs 'none' --seeds 3
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Stands if pIP10 <= 10 Hz and TN1 <= 2 Hz in >= 19 of 20 draws (P1's 50 / 8 far outside). Overturned if the median random draw gives pIP10 >= 25 Hz.

edge_cases.description: (a) P1 at 10, 60 and 100 Hz, 5 seeds, full male grid. (b) Subsets at 30 Hz: the 86 neurons whose MaleCNS synonyms name them pMP4/pMP-e (P1 proper), the other 62 pC1_* neurons, the right-hemisphere pC1_* only, and P1 + each hunger group (combined states).
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Nobody knows whether pIP10 has a threshold in P1 rate, or whether the song command needs the whole 45-type, 148-neuron cluster rather than P1 proper. The paper calls the group 'one class'. Real activation experiments drive a P1 split line of tens of neurons.
edge_cases.how_to_run: (a) wrapper W: for hz in 10 60 100; do mkdir -p experiments/results_edge/state_dose && FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore python3 -c "$W" experiments/results_edge/state_dose --dataset malecns --seeds 5 --state-hz $hz; done. (b) experiments/state_edge.py (spec in claim 1): FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 experiments/state_edge.py --dataset malecns --states 'none;courting male (P1/pC1 tonic);P1 pMP4 subset;P1 non-pMP4;P1 right;courting male (P1/pC1 tonic)+hungry (NPF tonic);courting male (P1/pC1 tonic)+fed (IPC tonic)' --inputs 'none;contact pheromone (ppk23/25);cVA (Or67d/DA1)' --seeds 5 --split --tag p1subsets
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Strengthens the claim if pIP10 rises monotonically from 10 Hz and the pMP4 subset alone gives pIP10 >= 20 Hz. If only the full 148-neuron cluster works, Note 6 should say 'the whole pC1/P1 cluster'. P1 + hunger within seed noise of P1 alone supports 'hunger changes nothing'.

edge_cases.description: P1 (and NPF / IPC) driven at 30 Hz in 1 globally rewired MaleCNS brain (rng 100, the Fig 6 male shuffle 0), inputs none and contact pheromone, 3 seeds.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: This completes the 'shuffle abolishes it' rule for the state arm. If the rewired brain still gives pIP10 > 10 Hz, pIP10 is being hit by P1's sheer output mass.
edge_cases.how_to_run: experiments/state_null.py: FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 experiments/state_null.py --dataset malecns --mode global --shuffles 1 --groups 'courting male (P1/pC1 tonic);hungry (NPF tonic);fed (IPC tonic)' --inputs 'none;contact pheromone (ppk23/25)' --seeds 3. Memory: the MaleCNS rewiring (25.6 M edges, several int64 copies) killed the 25 Sep re-run by swapping. Run it alone, only with swap use below about 1-2 GB, and skip it if the matched null already settled the question.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Passes if pIP10, TN1 and song MNs are <= 2 Hz in the shuffle while the intact rows reproduce 50 / 8 / 28.

claims.claim: Note 6: 'IPC, DH44, NPF, SIFa and AstA change no readout specifically (at most 7 Hz on MN9, as much as unrelated states)'. Main text: hunger neurons 'change nothing, in either sex', so 'the model draws a line between states by itself: the ones whose neurons act through synapses work, and the ones whose neurons act through chemistry do not'.
already_tested: 30 Hz, 5 seeds, both sexes, both lobes. Paper's model: largest |change| vs no state is female NPF 6.8 Hz (MN9 on sugar, 86.2+/-3.1 vs 79.4+/-3.4), IPC 3.2, DH44 3.0, SIFa 4.0, AstA 2.2; male 3.9-5.8 Hz (MDN with touch). The unrelated states SAG / pC1a-c / aIPg shift sugar -> MN9 to 83.0-83.8

100 Hz on the published lobe (3 seeds): the hunger rows show PPL1 +12-22 Hz with sugar, but only on seed 0. That is a bistable runaway that also hits SAG / pC1d/e and even 'none' (seed 4 at 30 Hz: 61 Hz), so it is not hunger-specific

New from existing files, no compute: at rest, hunger neurons recruit zero spikes anywhere. Total spikes = n_driven x rate exactly (AstA 56.4 = 2 x 28.2; NPF 114.6 = 4 x 28.65; IPC 493 = 18 x 27.4; DH44 173 = 6 x 28.9), in both sexes and at 100 Hz (at most about 37 extra spikes for SIFa). SAG (also 2 neurons) recruits about 320 spikes/s
Never tested: hunger with background activity (substrate), hunger at 100 Hz on the paper's model, hunger combined with SAG, held-out seeds

edge_cases.description: Full female and male state grids on the 0.2 Hz substrate (the 'hum'), 10 seeds, 1 s. Optional 10 s steady-state subset: states none / SAG / IPC / DH44 / NPF / SIFa / AstA x inputs none / sugar / touch, 5 seeds.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: 'Hunger changes nothing' was measured in a silent brain, and inhibition of a silent brain is invisible. Under the paper's known signs, AstA1 (known 'allatostatin-a; glutamate') and SIFa/DNc01-02 (known '...; glutamate') are inhibitory, and IPC/DH44/NPF are excitatory with outputs too weak to fire any neuron alone. With the substrate keeping the DNa at 15-20 Hz and neurons near threshold, sub-threshold hunger input could move feeding MNs, DNa (walking) or PPL1/PAM. The claim would then become 'nothing in a silent brain'. The SAG rows double as the offline counterpart of the arena virgin (DNp37 about 16 Hz).
edge_cases.how_to_run: No new file (runpy wrapper that also patches make_sim): cd . && WN='import sys,runpy,functools; sys.path.insert(0,"experiments"); import common; common.RES=sys.argv[1]; common.make_sim=functools.partial(common.make_sim, noise_hz=float(sys.argv[2])); sys.argv=["state_probe.py"]+sys.argv[3:]; runpy.run_path("experiments/state_probe.py", run_name="__main__")' && mkdir -p experiments/results_edge/state_noise0.2 && FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore python3 -c "$WN" experiments/results_edge/state_noise0.2 0.2 --dataset flywire --seeds 10 (then --dataset malecns --seeds 10 when memory allows). 10 s subset: experiments/state_edge.py --dataset flywire --noise-hz 0.2 --ms 10000 --seeds 5 --states 'none;virgin (SAG tonic);fed (IPC tonic);fed (DH44 tonic);hungry (NPF tonic);SIFa tonic;AstA tonic' --inputs 'none;sugar GRNs;touch (all head bristles)' --split --tag noise0.2_10s
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps the claim if every hunger state's |mean change| vs 'none' on the substrate stays within 2 x the seed s.e.m. and within the band of unrelated states on every readout (feed MNs, MN9, DNa L/R, PPL1, PAM, MDN). It must be qualified ('in a silent brain; on the hum, NPF/AstA ... by X Hz') if any hunger state moves a feeding or walking readout reproducibly by more than about 3 Hz and more than the unrelated states do. Also check that SAG on the substrate gives DNp37 near the arena's 15.8 Hz.

edge_cases.description: Hunger rows at 60 and 100 Hz on the paper's model. These come free from the female-sag-dose run (claim 1) and the male dose run (claim 2). The analysis adds recruited spikes and max |change| excluding the driven neurons.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The only 100 Hz evidence is the published lobe, whose seed-0 PPL1 runaways make 'nothing anywhere' (14w) literally false in that file (NPF + sugar PPL1 +21.9, SIFa +22.1). The paper's model has not been checked at high hunger drive.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Reuse experiments/results_edge/state_dose/state_probe_flywire_shiu_min1+known+eln0.25_state{60,100}.csv and state_probe_malecns_all_min1+eln0.25_state{60,100}.csv from the dose runs. Analysis in pandas with the same logic as paper_numbers.py lines 218-226 (max |delta| vs 'none', driven readouts excluded), plus total_spikes - n_driven*state readout at input none.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Stands if at 100 Hz every hunger state still recruits about 0 spikes at rest and its largest change is at most that of an unrelated state on the same cell. If NPF or IPC at 100 Hz wake any readout by > 5 Hz across all 10 seeds, the 'draws a line by itself' sentence needs 'at the rates tried'.

edge_cases.description: Female: SAG + NPF, SAG + IPC, SAG + AstA, SAG + DH44 (combined drive, 30 Hz each). Inputs none, touch, sugar and cVA, 10 seeds. Male P1 + hunger is covered in male-p1-dose-and-subsets.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Hunger could act through the social state even though it does nothing alone. In real flies starvation changes receptivity and courtship. If NPF or IPC changes the virgin's pC1a or vpoDN, 'hunger changes nothing' becomes 'hunger does nothing alone but modulates the virgin state'.
edge_cases.how_to_run: experiments/state_edge.py (spec in claim 1): FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 experiments/state_edge.py --dataset flywire --states 'none;virgin (SAG tonic);virgin (SAG tonic)+hungry (NPF tonic);virgin (SAG tonic)+fed (IPC tonic);virgin (SAG tonic)+AstA tonic;virgin (SAG tonic)+fed (DH44 tonic)' --inputs 'none;touch (all head bristles);sugar GRNs;cVA (Or67d/DA1)' --seeds 10 --split --tag sag_hunger
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Stands if pC1a, pC1b/c, DNp37 and touch-evoked pC1d/e under SAG + hunger stay within 2 s.e.m. of SAG alone (seeds are not paired across states, so compare means unpaired). A reproducible shift of > 3 Hz is a new result for the paper.

edge_cases.description: Seeds 5-9 (female, from the 30 Hz run of female-sag-dose) and seeds 5-14 (male, full grid) as held-out seeds for every Note 6 number, with the NPF +6.8 Hz MN9 shift and the 'unrelated states shift MN9 by 3.6-4.4' band tested at n = 10-15. Seeds 0-4 must reproduce the frozen file to the digit.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: MN9 on sugar has seed sd 3-7 Hz. With 5 seeds and about 20 readouts x 9 inputs x 5 states, a 6.8 Hz extreme is what multiple comparisons produce, and seeds are not paired across states (any extra drive shifts the RNG stream). 'At most 7 Hz' and 'as much as unrelated states' may both be noise.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Female: included in female-sag-dose (--state-hz 30 --seeds 10). Male: mkdir -p experiments/results_edge/state_heldout && FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore python3 -c "$W" experiments/results_edge/state_heldout --dataset malecns --seeds 15. NUMBA_NUM_THREADS must be 6 for the to-the-digit check (21b).
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Stands if the held-out means reproduce SAG 21 / 19 / 5.7, P1 50 / 8 / 28 within 2 s.e.m., and every hunger max |change| stays <= 7 Hz. Note 6 should then quote the pooled-seed numbers. If the NPF shift shrinks to the unrelated-state band or below, simplify to 'no hunger state changes any readout beyond seed noise'. If seeds 0-4 are not identical, record a thread or numba issue.

claims.claim: Note 6: 'DNp13 fires at 36 Hz virgin or mated, and oviDN stays at 0 under every state.' Main text: 'no state starts egg-laying and a mated female extends her ovipositor no more often than a virgin' (the model's two misses).
already_tested: 30 Hz, 5 seeds: touch -> DNp13 35.6-37.9 across all female states (paper_numbers)
Arena on the 0.2 Hz substrate: DNp13 on contact 31.7 (virgin) vs 30.6 (no state); oviDN 0.20 Hz in every substrate series, virgin or not, which is exactly the injected 0.2 Hz, i.e. no network drive
oviDN is 0.0 in every frozen offline file that records it (social probes, all state files including 100 Hz)

CONTRADICTING DATA ALREADY IN A FILE: published lobe at 100 Hz, 3 seeds, touch -> DNp13 is 36.3+/-1.5 with no state, 32.8+/-2.4 with SAG, and 29.0+/-0.9 with pC1a-c (29.5 / 29.5 / 28.0 vs 35 / 38 / 36, no overlap). 14w summarized this as 'unchanged by state (33-36 Hz)', leaving out the pC1a-c row
Never tested: the dose effect on DNp13 in the paper's model, and whether oviDN can fire at all (no positive control)

edge_cases.description: Touch and cVA + touch -> DNp13 under SAG and under pC1a-c tonic at 10-100 Hz, 10 seeds, paper's model. The data come from the female-sag-dose run; the analysis is an unpaired comparison of each state vs 'none' per rate.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The published lobe already shows the aroused state lowering DNp13 from 36 to 29 Hz at 100 Hz, in the direction real virgins show (they reject less). If the paper's model reproduces this, the 'state-blind rejection' miss becomes 'right direction, only at strong state drive'. Note 6's '36 Hz virgin or mated' then needs a rate qualifier.
edge_cases.how_to_run: Reuse experiments/results_edge/state_dose/state_probe_flywire_shiu_min1+known+eln0.25_state{10,20,30,60,100}.csv (female-sag-dose). pandas: for each rate, DNp13 mean +/- s.e.m. over 10 seeds for input 'touch (all head bristles)' and 'cVA + touch' under none, virgin (SAG tonic), aroused female (pC1a-c tonic); Welch t per cell.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keeps 'state-blind' if every state stays within 2 s.e.m. of 'none' at every rate. Qualifies it if SAG or pC1a-c at >= 60 Hz lowers touch -> DNp13 by > 3 Hz with p < 0.01. The paper would then say the model's rejection output does follow the virgin/aroused state, weakly and only at strong drive.

edge_cases.description: Can oviDN fire at all? Drive the top-5 excitatory presynaptic cell types of oviDN (by summed positive W onto oviDNa_a/oviDNa_b/oviDNb), each alone and all together, at 30 and 100 Hz, 3 seeds, with no input and with the 0.2 Hz substrate. Read oviDNa and oviDNb split.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: oviDN has never fired in any condition of the project. The substrate leaves it at exactly the injected 0.2 Hz, and no oviEN is labelled in FlyWire. If even its own strongest inputs cannot drive it, 'no state starts egg-laying' describes a readout the model cannot move and is not a state failure.
edge_cases.how_to_run: experiments/state_edge.py (spec in claim 1) with the --presyn-of option: FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 experiments/state_edge.py --dataset flywire --presyn-of 'oviDN egg' --top-types 5 --state-hz 30,100 --inputs none --seeds 3 --split --tag ovidn_reach; repeat with --noise-hz 0.2 --tag ovidn_reach_noise0.2. The script must print the 5 types with synapse counts and signs.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: If oviDN fires above 5 Hz from its own inputs, the claim stands as written: nothing the states reach connects to them. If oviDN stays <= 1 Hz even then, the paper should say 'the egg-laying neurons cannot be driven in this model, so the state arm cannot test egg-laying' instead of listing it as a state miss.

edge_cases.description: Model the mated state properly: on the 0.2 Hz substrate, compare no state, SAG output silenced (zeroed rows of W), and SAG 30 Hz. Inputs none, touch and cVA + touch, 10 seeds, 1 s. Read DNp13, DNp37, vpoEN, pC1a-e and oviDN split.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: In a silent brain 'mated = SAG silent' is identical to 'no state' by construction, so 'virgin or mated' is only a real comparison when SAG has background activity. On the substrate SAG fires at about 0.2 Hz. Silencing it could change the tonic pC1 / oviIN tone, which in real flies (SAG -> pC1 -> oviIN -| oviDN) is what disinhibits egg-laying after mating.
edge_cases.how_to_run: experiments/state_edge.py: FLYBRAIN_SIGNS=known FLYBRAIN_ELN=0.25 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 python3 experiments/state_edge.py --dataset flywire --noise-hz 0.2 --states 'none;virgin (SAG tonic)' --inputs 'none;touch (all head bristles);cVA + touch' --seeds 10 --split --tag mated_noise0.2, then the same with --silence 'virgin (SAG tonic)' --states 'none' --tag mated_silenced_noise0.2
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Expected pass: silenced equals no state within noise on every readout, which confirms 'mated = baseline'. Any reproducible difference (> 2 s.e.m.) in DNp13 or oviDN between silenced and baseline would be a new, testable prediction.

claims.claim: Note 6: 'The state results are identical under both smell-centre settings' (published lobe vs the paper's eLN x0.25 + known signs).
already_tested: State-alone cells (input none): max |published - paper| = 0.3 Hz female (aIPg -> DNa L), 0.0 male; paper_numbers checks SAG and P1 alone 'X -> X'
The notes (19e, 19e-m) themselves record that state x odour cells differ and withdraw two remarks because of it

edge_cases.description: No simulation. Add a check to paper_numbers.py (or a pandas one-off) that counts state-row cells differing by > 1 Hz between the two settings, split into input none, odour inputs and non-odour inputs. Use it to scope the sentence.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: From the frozen files, 333 of 810 female state x odour cells and 397 of 840 male ones differ by > 1 Hz. Examples: SAG + cVA + touch -> pC1d/e 1.0 vs 7.1; SAG + cVA -> pC1a 17.5 vs 21.5; P1 + food -> MN9 19.4 vs 2.6, pIP10 40.7 vs 49.1; PPL1 up to 109-122 Hz. notes:
TEXT VS RESULTS (all from the frozen pre_rerun_20260926 files; nothing was run):
1. 'vpoDN 5.7 Hz' is probably mislabelled. The readout 'vpoEN/DN accept' pools 4 vpoEN and 2 DNp37 (common.py line 74; figures_print labels it 'vpoEN/vpoDN'). Pooled seed values x6 give 43/35/44/24/26 spikes. If vpoEN is silent, vpoDN (DNp37) fires about 17 Hz, which matches the arena's DNp37-only readout (motor.py 'accept' = ^DNp37$) of 15.8-15.9 Hz. Confirm with the split run (cheapest decisive test), then fix Note 6, paper_numbers label 'SAG tonic alone -> vpoDN' and Fig 5.
2. 'DNp13 state-blind': the published 100 Hz file (3 seeds) has pC1a-c -> touch DNp13 29.0+/-0.9 and SAG 32.8+/-2.4 vs 36.3+/-1.5 with no state. 14w summarized this as 'unchanged (33-36 Hz)', which leaves out the pC1a-c row. This can qualify one of the paper's two stated misses, in the biologically right direction.
3. 14w 'hunger neurons at 100 Hz: still nothing anywhere' is literally false in that file. Seed-0 PPL1 runaways with sugar (+12-22 Hz) appear in hunger rows, in unrelated states, and even in 'none' at 30 Hz published (seed 4: 61 Hz). So the effect is not hunger-specific, but the wording should not be quoted.
4. 'Identical under both smell-centre settings' holds only for the state-alone rows (max 0.3 Hz). Many state x odour cells differ, and some non-odour ones too (male P1 + sugar PPL1 by 91.5 Hz).
5. 'Song motor neurons 28 Hz' is not state-specific. Without any state, contact pheromone alone drives the song MNs at 21.3 Hz and all pheromones + contact + touch at 30.9 Hz (higher than P1's 27.6). The state-specific signatures are pIP10 (0 -> 50) and TN1 (0 -> 8).
6. A strong new fact is available at no compute cost: hunger/satiety neurons recruit zero spikes anywhere at rest. Total spikes equal n_driven x rate exactly at 30 Hz in both sexes, and essentially at 100 Hz too. SAG, also 2 neurons, recruits about 320 spikes/s. This supports the paper's line better than '<= 7 Hz on MN9'.
7. The 'synapses vs chemistry' line has two caveats. (a) SAG (FlyWire AN_SMP_2, 2 neurons) has no known transmitter; its predicted top_nt is serotonin at 0.47 / 0.52 confidence, made excitatory by Shiu's rule, so the virgin result's sign rests on a low-confidence prediction. This is consistent with the behavioural literature but should be stated. (b) Under the paper's known signs, AstA1 and SIFa (DNc01/02) are glutamatergic, i.e. inhibitory, and inhibition is invisible in a silent brain. That is why the hum test (hunger-on-substrate) is priority 1.
8. The 'one class' wording is generous for P1: the male state is all 148 pC1_* neurons of 45 types; 86 of them carry the pMP4/pMP-e synonym.
9. pC1a follows SAG at about 0.75 spikes per SAG spike at both 30 and 100 Hz: a near one-to-one relay from 2 neurons. The gain-0.7 test is the most likely place for the virgin result to fail.

claims.claim: Note 7: 'Sugar, bitter and touch drive 0.0 Hz in every dopamine neuron, so the teaching signal drives the identified reward (PAM) or punishment (PPL1) set at 50 Hz when the fly tastes sugar or bitter.' The main text says the same: 'sugar and bitter tastes never reach the teaching neurons'.
evidence_files: RESEARCH_NOTES.md (16d uses 'scratch us_probe'; that script is not in the repo)
already_tested: Female, 5 seeds, gain 1.0 (social probe): sugar, bitter and touch give exactly 0.0 Hz as group means in PAM and PPL1.

Gain sweep, 5 seeds: sugar and touch give exactly 0 at gains 0.5, 0.7 and 1.0. At gain 1.4 touch gives PPL1 0.10 Hz. At gain 2.0 (runaway) sugar gives PAM 0.34 / PPL1 8.1 Hz and touch gives 0.86 / 18.5 Hz.
With the 0.2 Hz hum, sugar gives PPL1 2.5 Hz and touch 3.1 Hz. That is background activity and says nothing about taste.
In the rewired brain sugar drives about 0.
In context, sugar GRNs at 100 Hz on top of the CS+ served as the US (--us wiring, n=4). The index was 0.03 +/- 0.04, the same as no US.

Not tested: bitter across gains, bitter or touch together with an odour, the per-type claim (the result files store only PAM and PPL1 group means; per-type 0.0 comes from scratch us_probe), and the male. The male's pooled labellar GRNs drive PPL1 at 11.7 Hz at gain 1.0 and 54 Hz at 1.4 (18b), so 'every dopamine neuron at 0.0' is a female-only statement.

edge_cases.description: Use the fly's own taste channels as the US while the CS+ is on: bitter GRNs + CS+ and head bristles + CS+ (female, both odour orders, seed 0), and the male's pooled labellar GRNs + CS+ (both orders). Compare the taught-compartment index and the logged DAN rate during 'CS+ & US' with the existing sugar-wiring no-US runs.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: While an odour is on, the DANs are already near threshold (vinegar drives PPL106 at 25 Hz and PPL107 at 87 Hz), so a bitter or touch input that is silent alone could tip PPL1 over. In the male, taste already drives PPL1 at 12 Hz, so there the wiring may carry a teaching signal after all, and it would be punishment for a sugar-paired odour.
edge_cases.how_to_run: New code: experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py (a copy of experiments/conditioning.py; spec under contingency-controls) with --wiring-us {sugar,bitter,touch,labellar}. sugar = gustatory & sub_class 'sugar/water'; bitter = gustatory & '^bitter$'; touch = cell_type '^BM_'; labellar = gustatory & 'sugar/water|labellar bristle'. It prints the size of the US group and aborts if it is 0. Runs: for o in 'vinegar ester' 'ester vinegar'; do set -- $o; for w in bitter touch; do python3 experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py --dataset flywire --signs known --eln 0.25 --us wiring --wiring-us $w --valence punish --csp $1 --csm $2 --seed 0 --out-dir experiments/results_edge; done; python3 experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py --dataset malecns --eln 0.25 --us wiring --wiring-us labellar --valence punish --csp $1 --csm $2 --seed 0 --out-dir experiments/results_edge; done. (--valence only picks which compartment the summary treats as taught; with --us wiring it adds no US.)
edge_cases.pass_criterion: The claim holds if, for bitter and touch in both orders, the punishment-compartment index is within +/-0.05 of the sugar-wiring no-US run of the same order and the DAN rate during 'CS+ & US' is within 1 Hz of the rate in the CS- phase. If the male's labellar-GRN US takes the CS+ punishment-compartment drive more than 0.15 below its no-US level, Note 7 has to say 'female', and state that the male's own taste reaches the punishment DANs and writes an aversive memory for a food-paired odour.

edge_cases.description: Re-read taste to DAN, bitter included, at gain 0.7 and 1.4 and at a 200 Hz taste drive, using the existing social probe with its output redirected.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Bitter was measured only at gain 1.0 and 100 Hz. The group means are rounded, and touch already gives PPL1 0.10 Hz at gain 1.4.
