claims.claim: Note 7: 'Offline, in the design of Tully & Quinn (three cycles of 10 s), the paired odour keeps 0.10-0.11 of its drive and the other 0.59-0.66: learning index 0.54 +/- 0.02 (n=6)'. The robustness rows (18f): US at 20 Hz gives 0.56 +/- 0.04, eLN x0.1 gives 0.62 +/- 0.02. Main text: 'the smell that came with sugar reached the output neurons at a tenth of its old strength, while the other smell kept about three-fifths'.
already_tested: Both odour orders x 3 seeds. The seeds change only Poisson timing (noise_hz = 0), so n=6 is 2 designs x 3 timing replicates.
US at 20 Hz (n=6): 0.56. eLN x0.1 (n=6): 0.62. Phasic US with tau_dan 2 (n=2): 0.54 and 0.66.

Recomputed from the frozen files: CS+ 0.095-0.107, CS- 0.59-0.70, index 0.55 +/- 0.03. The paper's '0.54 +/- 0.02' and '0.59-0.66' are stale. paper_numbers.py marks them 'ok' only because same() allows 0.55 absolute tolerance.
Training log: most of the taught-compartment loss happens in cycle 1 (reward-comp weight 0.953 after cycle 1, 0.944 after cycle 3), so the CS+ is at the 0.10 floor well before three pairings.
Not tested: training length, learning rate, the floor, the eligibility window, any odour pair other than vinegar/ester, and US doses below 20 Hz.

edge_cases.description: Learning curve and learning-rate sweep. Reward US: cycles 1 and 10 at eta 0.3, and eta 0.1 and 1.0 at 3 cycles. Add matched no-US runs (--us wiring) at cycles 10 and at eta 1.0. Both odour orders, seed 0, 12 runs. Record the taught-compartment drive retained for CS+ and CS-, the index, and the post-pre DN changes.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The CS+ saturates at the floor within cycle 1. The CS- keeps losing drive in two ways: through shared KCs, which saturates, and through its own tonic odour-evoked dopamine, which grows linearly with eta x time. So the index should shrink with longer training or a larger eta, and could head toward 0. 'Odour-specific' would then describe only short, low-rate training. The constants are ours (Note 7).
edge_cases.how_to_run: After the re-run queue has finished, never alongside it. cd . && mkdir -p experiments/results_edge; ce() { NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 -c "import sys,runpy; sys.path.insert(0,'experiments'); import common; common.RES='experiments/results_edge'; sys.argv=['experiments/conditioning.py']+sys.argv[1:]; runpy.run_path('experiments/conditioning.py', run_name='__main__')" "$@"; }; B='--dataset flywire --signs known --eln 0.25 --seed 0'; for o in 'vinegar ester' 'ester vinegar'; do set -- $o; ce $B --us dan --valence reward --cycles 1 --csp $1 --csm $2 --tag cyc1; ce $B --us dan --valence reward --cycles 10 --csp $1 --csm $2 --tag cyc10; ce $B --us wiring --cycles 10 --csp $1 --csm $2 --tag cyc10; ce $B --us dan --valence reward --eta 0.1 --csp $1 --csm $2 --tag eta0.1; ce $B --us dan --valence reward --eta 1.0 --csp $1 --csm $2 --tag eta1.0; ce $B --us wiring --eta 1.0 --csp $1 --csm $2 --tag eta1.0; done. Every flag is in conditioning.py's argparse. --tag is needed because eta and cycles are not in the automatic tag. The output must not go to experiments/results: paper_numbers.py groups files by rsplit('_seed') and would silently pool tagged files into the paper's indices.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Keep 'odour-specific' if the index is >= 0.3 in both orders at cycles 10 and at eta 1.0, and at least 0.2 above the matched no-US run. Then state that the CS+ number is the floor, reached within one pairing. If the index falls below 0.2 at 10 cycles or at eta 1.0, the paper has to say that the model's own odour-driven dopamine erodes the CS- and specificity holds only for short training. Non-expression is kept if the CS+-specific DN change relative to the no-US run (post-pre CS+ minus CS-) stays under 2 Hz at eta 1.0 and cycles 10.

edge_cases.description: Two more pairs from the library, chosen by glomerular overlap. sweet vs ester share 4 of 6 glomeruli (VM2, DM2, VA2, DM4): the hardest discrimination. floral vs vinegar share none. Both orders, reward US plus a no-US run each, seed 0, 8 runs.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: '0.54 +/- 0.02' comes from one pair; the +/- is Poisson timing only. The index is roughly 1 minus the generalisation to the CS- minus the floor, and generalisation follows KC overlap (the index rose to 0.62 at eLN x0.1 when overlap fell). A high-overlap pair could land near 0.1-0.2, and a zero-overlap pair near 0.8.
edge_cases.how_to_run: ce and B as in training-length-and-rate-erosion; for p in 'sweet ester' 'ester sweet' 'floral vinegar' 'vinegar floral'; do set -- $p; ce $B --us dan --valence reward --csp $1 --csm $2; ce $B --us wiring --csp $1 --csm $2; done. --csp/--csm take any ODOR_LIBRARY class (brain/flybrain/senses.py: ester, vinegar, floral, green, sweet, aversive). Sanity check in the log: 'CS+ floral: N ORNs' with N > 100 and pre-test KC >= 1 %. If floral recruits under 1 % of KCs, use green instead.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: The claim generalises if the appetitive index is >= 0.3 in all four new orders and the no-US runs are <= 0.1. The paper then reports the index as a range over three pairs, not as '0.54 +/- 0.02'. If sweet/ester gives < 0.2, the paper must say that specificity depends on how many Kenyon cells the two odours share, and give the range.

edge_cases.description: Floor w_min at 0 and 0.3 (default 0.1). KC eligibility trace tau_elig at 0.2 s and 3 s (default 1 s). Reward US, both orders, seed 0, 8 runs, with DN readouts.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: 'Keeps 0.10-0.11 of its drive' is the floor constant, not a measurement. At floor 0.3 the index drops by about 0.2, and the CS- may reach the floor as well. A longer trace spreads depression onto the CS- (the rests are 5 s). At floor 0 the CS+ drive in the taught compartments goes to zero, which is the largest memory the model can hold, so it is the natural setting to re-check 'no DN changes'.
edge_cases.how_to_run: New code in experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py: --w-min (float, default 0.1, passed to PlasticityConfig(w_min=...)) and --tau-elig (float, default 1.0, passed as tau_elig), both written into the tag. for o in 'vinegar ester' 'ester vinegar'; do set -- $o; for x in '--w-min 0' '--w-min 0.3' '--tau-elig 0.2' '--tau-elig 3'; do python3 experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py --dataset flywire --signs known --eln 0.25 --us dan --valence reward --csp $1 --csm $2 --seed 0 $x --out-dir experiments/results_edge; done; done
edge_cases.pass_criterion: The claim survives if the index stays >= 0.3 at every setting (expected about 0.65 at floor 0 and about 0.35 at floor 0.3) and the CS-/CS+ ordering never flips. Whatever happens, the main text should call the tenth 'the floor I set'. At floor 0, non-expression holds if every DN readout (DNa L/R, DNp09, MDN, feed MNs, DN all) has a CS+-specific change under 2 Hz beyond the no-US run.

edge_cases.description: Reward US at 2, 5 and 100 Hz (20 and 50 already exist). Both orders, seed 0, 6 runs.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: 20 and 50 Hz both saturate the CS+ at the floor, so the 'robust to US dose' row cannot show a dose-response. The low end shows where the memory becomes graded. At 100 Hz the 150 PAMs run near their refractory limit and could spill into non-US compartments, eroding the CS-.

edge_cases.pass_criterion: The claim holds if the index is >= 0.3 at 5 Hz and within +/-0.1 of 0.55 at 100 Hz. Report the lowest dose at which the CS+ reaches the floor. If 100 Hz drops the index below 0.4, the dose row needs an upper bound.

edge_cases.description: Seeds 3 and 4 of the main appetitive design, both orders.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: It is unlikely to break anything: seeds only reshuffle Poisson timing, and the spread across seeds is 0.02-0.03. Listed for completeness. The odour-pair test is the real held-out test.

edge_cases.pass_criterion: Index within 0.55 +/- 0.06 for all four runs.

claims.claim: Note 7: '0.04 without a teaching signal'. The index is associative: the no-US control uses --us wiring, where sugar GRNs reach no DAN.
already_tested: No-US control, n=4 but unbalanced: 3 seeds with vinegar as CS+ and 1 with ester as CS+. Reward-compartment index -0.014, 0.024, 0.040, 0.084, so 0.03 +/- 0.04. The paper's '0.04' is stale.
Phasic no-US (tau_dan 2): 0.06.
Missing: backward pairing, unpaired presentation, US alone, and extinction. The only contingency control is 'no US at all'.

edge_cases.description: The standard fly controls. Backward: US alone for 10 s, then CS+ alone for 10 s straight after. Unpaired: CS+ alone, 5 s rest, US alone. US-only: the US with no CS+ during training. Each has a CS- block per cycle, 3 cycles. Reward US in both orders (6 runs) plus backward with the punishment US in both orders (2 runs).
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The rule has a KC trace but no DAN trace, so backward and unpaired should give about 0. If they don't, some of the index is not contiguity. Possible reasons: DAN activity outlasting the US through recurrent DAN/MBON loops, PAM-to-KC synapses making KCs eligible during the US, or US-driven non-specific depression that happens to hit the CS+ harder. US-only measures directly how much of the CS- loss (0.30-0.40) the US causes by itself, which also tests the 'generalisation through shared KCs' reading in 16f.
edge_cases.how_to_run: New file experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py: a copy of experiments/conditioning.py plus --out-dir (default experiments/results_edge), --w-min, --tau-elig, --wiring-us, and --protocol {forward,backward,unpaired,us-only,trace,extinction} with --gap-s and --ext-cycles. Phase lists per cycle: forward [CS+&US T | rest R | CS- T | rest R]; backward [US T | CS+ T | rest R | CS- T | rest R]; unpaired [CS+ T | rest R | US T | rest R | CS- T | rest R]; us-only [US T | rest R | CS- T | rest R]; trace [CS+ T | gap G (no drive) | US T | rest R | CS- T | rest R]; extinction = forward x cycles, then a mid test, then ext-cycles x [CS+ T | rest R | CS- T | rest R]. 'US' is pl.us_drive(...) for --us dan, or the --wiring-us group at 100 Hz. The tag encodes every non-default argument; a JSON sidecar records all args. The CSV schema matches conditioning.py (extinction adds 'mid_*' columns). Runs: for o in 'vinegar ester' 'ester vinegar'; do set -- $o; for p in backward unpaired us-only; do python3 experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py --dataset flywire --signs known --eln 0.25 --us dan --valence reward --protocol $p --csp $1 --csm $2 --seed 0; done; python3 experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py --dataset flywire --signs known --eln 0.25 --us dan --valence punish --protocol backward --csp $1 --csm $2 --seed 0; done
edge_cases.pass_criterion: 'Associative' holds if the backward and unpaired indices are within 0.1 of the no-US index (0.03) in both orders, and US-only leaves both odours' taught-compartment drive >= 0.85. If backward or unpaired gives > 0.2, or US-only takes either odour below 0.8, the paper must say part of the index comes from the US itself, not from pairing, and reduce the associative share accordingly.

edge_cases.description: Add seeds 1 and 2 of the ester-as-CS+ no-US run, so the control matches the 3+3 design of the US runs.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The control currently has 3 vinegar+ runs and 1 ester+ run. In the punishment compartment the two orders go in opposite directions (+0.26 to +0.32 against -0.24), so the pooled no-US value depends on the imbalance.
edge_cases.how_to_run: ce as above; for s in 1 2; do ce --dataset flywire --signs known --eln 0.25 --us wiring --csp ester --csm vinegar --seed $s; done
edge_cases.pass_criterion: With the 3+3 design, the reward-compartment no-US index should stay <= 0.1. Report no-US per order and per compartment rather than as one pooled number.

edge_cases.description: Extinction: 3 forward cycles, then 3 cycles of CS+ alone and CS- alone with plasticity on, tested before and after. Trace conditioning: US starts 0.5, 1 or 3 s after CS+ offset. Reward US, vinegar+/ester-, seed 0.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Offline the rule only depresses and tau_rec = 0, so extinction is impossible by construction and further CS- exposure can only erode the index. In the world the server uses the default tau_rec = 600 s. The trace test shows that tau_elig alone sets the timing window. Both runs mostly document limits of the model, not risks to a claim.
edge_cases.how_to_run: python3 experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py --dataset flywire --signs known --eln 0.25 --us dan --valence reward --protocol extinction --ext-cycles 3 --csp vinegar --csm ester --seed 0; for g in 0.5 1 3; do python3 experiments/edge/conditioning_edge.py --dataset flywire --signs known --eln 0.25 --us dan --valence reward --protocol trace --gap-s $g --csp vinegar --csm ester --seed 0; done
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Expected result: the CS+ stays at the floor after extinction, the CS- falls at the exposure-only rate, and the trace index follows roughly exp(-gap/1 s). The paper should add one sentence saying the offline rule has no extinction or forgetting. Nothing in Note 7 changes unless the trace index stays above 0.3 at a 3 s gap, which would point to a DAN or KC persistence that needs explaining.

claims.claim: Note 7: 'learning index 0.21 +/- 0.14 for punishment' (aversive; the punishment US drives the PPL1 set at 50 Hz). 18f adds 20 Hz: 0.23 and eLN x0.1: 0.26.
already_tested: Both orders x 3 seeds. The mean of 0.2125 hides two groups: vinegar as CS+ gives 0.30-0.38, ester as CS+ gives 0.07-0.08.
20 Hz and eLN x0.1 (n=2 each), and phasic US (n=3).

The paper sets it beside the reward-compartment no-US value (0.04). The right control is the punishment-compartment no-US value per order. That is +0.26 to +0.32 with vinegar as CS+ and -0.24 with ester as CS+, because vinegar depresses its own punishment input through tonic PPL1. The associative increment over the matched control is only +0.07 with vinegar as CS+ and +0.31 with ester as CS+ (computed from the frozen files).

edge_cases.description: Re-analysis with no simulation. For each order, compute the punishment-compartment index minus the matched no-US index for the same order and compartment. Do the same for the 20 Hz, eLN x0.1 and phasic rows. Add it to paper_numbers.py section K as 'associative increment'.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: This already qualifies the claim. For vinegar as CS+ the aversive memory is mostly vinegar punishing itself, and a pooled 0.21 +/- 0.14 hides that.

Expression probe (3 seeds, 1 s): tonic 0/5/10/20/40 Hz on the targets, MBONs intact or silenced, odour none/left/both. Reward set: silencing shifts DNa by 1-5 Hz; DNp09/MDN/feed stay at 0. Punishment set at tonic 0 under bilateral odour: its 28 DN targets are 6.99 vs 7.14 Hz.

Design flaw 2: a kicked target cannot be inhibited, so the disinhibition the appetitive memory relies on (inhibitory reward MBONs) cannot show up in the kicked targets at all.

No result file drives the MBONs themselves. notes:
I ran no simulations and changed no files. All values below were recomputed from release/pre_rerun_20260926/results and logs/learn_world{4,5,6}_probe_*.json.

WHERE THE PAPER TEXT DISAGREES WITH THE RESULT FILES
1. Stale numbers. The frozen files give index 0.55 +/- 0.03, not 0.54 +/- 0.02. They give CS- 0.59-0.70 (ester-vs-vinegar seed0 CS- = 0.697), not 0.59-0.66. They give no-US 0.03 (0.033), not 0.04.

2. The number checker cannot catch errors of this size. same() in experiments/paper_numbers.py accepts any difference up to 0.55 absolute (or 3 %). Every number below about 1 passes whatever its value: '0.54' would pass against a computed 0.00. This covers indices, retained fractions, freeze indices, Jaccard values and walk duty. So 'a script checks 155 numbers and none differ' is empty for all fraction-scale numbers. Fix: tolerate half a unit of the last printed digit.

3. The in-world aversive 0.29 is not learning. world6 had sugar only and no bitter anywhere, and its punishment-compartment ester-minus-vinegar value is 0.31 (0.438 vs 0.131). world5, with bitter on vinegar, gives 0.29. The number is vinegar's tonic PPL1 punishing its own input. Drop '0.29 with bitter' as written, or pair it with the world6 control.

4. The offline aversive index is compared with the wrong control. '0.21 +/- 0.14' sits beside the reward-compartment no-US value (0.04). Its own control, the punishment compartment per order, is +0.26 to +0.32 (vinegar as CS+) and -0.24 (ester as CS+). The associative increment is +0.07 with vinegar as CS+ and +0.31 with ester as CS+. The no-US design is also unbalanced: 3 vinegar+ seeds against 1 ester+.

5. 'Reward output neurons, driven at 40 Hz, reach none' matches no result file. expression_probe.py drives the MBONs' targets, not the MBONs. The only MBON-drive data is 16f's scratch 'mbon_dn' (30 and 60 Hz), which is not in the repo. 16d's per-type 'sugar/bitter/touch 0.0 Hz in every PAM and PPL1 type' is also scratch-only; the result files hold only group means, which are exactly 0 at gain <= 1.0 for sugar and touch.

6. 'No working route to the neurons that move the fly' (main text) contradicts 16f. MBON14 alone at 30 Hz drives DNa L 14 / R 7 and DNge053 35, DNbe007 27, DNb05 26, DNg100 24 Hz. The data supports a weaker claim: the odour drives the MBONs only weakly (reward set 0.5 Hz with odour on one antenna, 6.2 Hz bilaterally, 0.0 Hz reward-compartment response to ester before training; punishment set 5-12 Hz), and depression can only remove that. The notebook's pages are nearly blank, as well as unread.

7. The expression probe has two design flaws. (a) Its 28 readout DNs are inside the tonic-driven set. Every tonic event is a 68.75 mV kick that fires the neuron, so those DNs sit at the injected rate (10.7 / 14.8 / 22.8 / 38.6 Hz at 5 / 10 / 20 / 40), and 'within 0.6 Hz intact vs silenced' is true by construction except at tonic 0 (7.0 vs 7.1). (b) Kicked targets cannot be inhibited, so the disinhibition test for the inhibitory reward MBONs was structurally unable to succeed. This undercuts 18g's verdict that tonic activity does not rescue expression.

8. 'No descending neuron changes with training' is literally false. DNa L/R change by up to 7.5 Hz with training. The change is identical with no US, so the accurate wording is 'no DN change depends on the pairing'.

9. 'A tenth of its old strength' is the floor constant w_min = 0.1, not a measurement. The training log shows the taught compartment saturating within cycle 1 (0.953 after cycle 1, 0.944 after cycle 3).

10. The male breaks the '0.0 Hz' statement. His pooled labellar GRNs drive PPL1 at 11.7 Hz at gain 1.0 and 54 Hz at 1.4 (gain_sweep_malecns; 18b), so Note 7's '0.0 Hz in every dopamine neuron' holds for the female only. The male learning result (n=2 per valence, seed 0) also has no no-US control.

11. Smaller points:
- Offline runs use tau_rec = 0. The world brain uses PlasticityConfig's default tau_rec = 600 s (server.py does not override it), so the in-world rule includes recovery and is not the offline rule.
- Tully & Quinn 1985 trained once for 60 s with 12 shocks. 'Three cycles of 10 s' is not their design.
- Seeds only reshuffle Poisson timing (noise_hz 0), so '+/- 0.02, n=6' is 2 designs x 3 timing replicates, with one odour pair.

SCRIPT PITFALLS FOR THE RUN PHASE
- conditioning.py writes to common.RES = experiments/results, which the re-run is rewriting live. paper_numbers.py groups conditioning files by base.rsplit('_seed', 1)[0], so a tagged edge file such as ..._seed0_cyc10.csv would be silently pooled into the paper's indices. Redirect output with the inline runner 'ce' (no file edits needed): ce() { NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6 $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 -c "import sys,runpy; sys.path.insert(0,'experiments'); import common; common.RES='experiments/results_edge'; sys.argv=['experiments/conditioning.py']+sys.argv[1:]; runpy.run_path('experiments/conditioning.py', run_name='__main__')" "$@"; } (run from the project root).
- eta and cycles are not in conditioning.py's automatic tag; use --tag.
- conditioning.py's SUGAR selector ('sugar/water') may be empty in MaleCNS, and the script never prints its size.
- New code (conditioning_edge.py, expression_harsh.py) should go in new files under experiments/edge/. Do not edit conditioning.py, lif.py or plasticity.py while the re-run queue can still execute them.

HARDWARE PLAN
- Start only after the re-run queue (logs/rerun_20260926_steps.tsv) finishes. Conditioning and expression are near its end.
- Queue the edge steps through experiments/run_guarded.sh with their own step file and DONE dir. Gate at >= 25 % free memory for female runs and >= 30 % for male runs, NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=6, one process at a time.
- Memory: female runs peak at about 1.5 GB (core-check 1.5 GB, odor-code 1.4 GB in logs/guarded_peaks.tsv). Allow about 3.5 GB for male runs. An arena run means server (-Xmx2G) + brain + node, about 5 GB, and must run alone. Swap already shows 5.9 GB used under the current queue.

5 + 5 original trials and 5 + 5 replication trials (600 s)
stop-on-contact hum row offline (0.77-0.90)
male MDN on contact 29-48 Hz in every chamber

edge_cases.description: Re-run the hum female pair with a synchronised start, new seeds and distinct seeds per fly, at 600 s on an idle machine (~170 s brain). This removes the launch-stagger artefact, gives an independent sample and doubles as the 'longer trials' check.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: 2 of the 5 replication ff trials (t1, t3) touched within 4-7 ticks because fly1 walked to fly2's spawn. Original and replication also disagree fivefold on contact % (11 vs 59 %). Bout durations are short: median 0.3 s (orig) and 0.85 s (rep), with only 9-11 % of bouts over 5 s. So 'stayed together' may be a start artefact plus a few long pauses.
edge_cases.how_to_run: New code: (a) bot/bot.js option --waitFor=<name>. In the spawn handler, after buildArena and /tp, poll every 100 ms until bot.players[<name>]?.entity exists, re-send the same /tp, wait 500 ms, and only then start the --duration timer, the Observer and connectBrain(). (b) experiments/run_pair.sh: add ${SYNC:+--waitFor=fly2} to fly1's node line and ${SYNC:+--waitFor=fly1} to fly2's. (c) experiments/trials.sh: pass --seed "$(( ${SEED0:-0} + i ))" and export SEED2=$(( ${SEED0:-0} + i + 1000 )). In run_pair.sh fly2's python line, append ${SEED2:+--seed "$SEED2"} after "$@" (argparse keeps the last --seed). Then, with the server up: SYNC=1 SEED0=100 CONDS=ff NOISE=0.2 LABEL=sync-noise0.2 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=3 caffeinate -i experiments/encounter_trials.sh 5 600 ; $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 experiments/encounter_stats.py --chamber sync-noise0.2 > logs/edge_sync-noise0.2_stats.out ; $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 experiments/replication_stats.py --prefix sync- --out experiments/results/edge_sync_noise0.2.md
edge_cases.pass_criterion: The claim holds if >= 3/5 trials have a first contact >= 2 s after both flies are present, on-contact DNa <= 3 Hz, and at least one bout >= 10 s. It narrows to 'meet and pause for seconds' if meetings occur but no bout exceeds ~5 s. It is overturned if <= 1/5 trials meet. Report contact % with n = 5 pairs, not 10 fly-logs, since both flies share the contact ticks.

edge_cases.description: Female pairs at hum 0.1 and 0.3 Hz, to test whether 'meet and stay' is specific to the 0.2 Hz the author chose.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: Bout end is noise-driven DNa recovery against touch suppression, and at 0.3 Hz the giant fibre fires ~7 Hz (19c), so jumps may break every contact. At 0.1 the steady-state DNa is already 17/19 Hz, so walking stays but meetings may change.
edge_cases.how_to_run: With the server up: CONDS=ff NOISE=0.1 LABEL=noise0.1 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=3 caffeinate -i experiments/encounter_trials.sh 5 300 ; CONDS=ff NOISE=0.3 LABEL=noise0.3 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=3 caffeinate -i experiments/encounter_trials.sh 5 300 ; then encounter_stats.py --chamber noise0.1 and --chamber noise0.3, plus lean_check.py --chambers noise0.1,noise0.3. Prefix SYNC=1 SEED0=200 once sync-hum-ff's code exists. Otherwise flag t1/t3 with start_check.py.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: The result is not level-specific if at both levels >= 2/5 trials have a genuine meeting, with on-contact DNa <= 3 Hz and at least one bout >= 5 s. If bouts collapse at 0.3 (all < 2 s) or no one meets at 0.1, the paper must say 'at 0.2 Hz' and that staying depends on the hum level. Brain time must be >= 60 s per log, since the 0.3 Hz brains run slower.

claims.claim: Note 8: nobody sings or fights (P1/pIP10 at the injected 0.2 Hz near, far and on contact; lunges at the hum floor of 2-3 a minute).
already_tested: floors measured in every hum series
offline: pC1a-e, aIPg, vpoDN and oviDN at 0.0 Hz for every input, at every gain and in 14 conditions; male P1 <= 0.6 Hz
state arm: P1 tonic -> pIP10 50 Hz (the song path works when driven)

edge_cases.description: A male-male pair on the hum. This was never run, and it is the pairing in which real flies fight.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: 'Nobody fights' has so far been tested only with females present. Male-male contact gives cVA plus ppk23 in both brains, a combination never presented in the arena.
edge_cases.how_to_run: encounter_trials.sh cannot do this: CONDS accepts only ff/mf, DS2 is fixed to flywire, and it overwrites BRAIN_ARGS when NOISE != 0. Call trials.sh directly with the server up: node experiments/survey_chamber.js --port 25565 --radius 45 --clear ; NO_FOOD=1 VIEW1=0 VIEW2=0 ARENA_R=6 ARENA_Y=64 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=3 DS1=malecns DS2=malecns LABEL=mm-noise0.2 BRAIN_ARGS='--noise-hz 0.2' caffeinate -i experiments/trials.sh off 5 300 ; $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 experiments/encounter_stats.py --chamber mm-noise0.2. It prints only the male block, and the distinct label keeps these males apart from the mf males. Without NO_FOOD=1 the arena is built with flowers, honey and cake.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: The claim extends to males if attack events per minute near and on contact stay at the hum floor, P1/pIP10 stay at 0.2 Hz, and contact ends with MDN backing. Lunging above the floor would make 'nobody fights' pairing-specific. Caveat for the text: the aggression readout is the female-defined pC1d/e + aIPg group, so a null in males is weak evidence. Two MaleCNS brains need an idle machine (>= 60 % free).

claims.claim: Note 9: nobody walks towards anybody. The turn-toward index is -0.02 to +0.03 (original) and 0.00 to +0.04 (replication). The one trace: pooled over every series, the female leans towards the male in 24 of 33 male-female recordings (sign test p = 0.014, pooled +0.015 = 6 % of her turning, 'about the size of the pull his pheromone has'); female pairs 13/9 (p = 0.52).
already_tested: per-series toward index (Table 1)
pre-contact distance bins (19b, 21b)
per-log sign-flip for the virgin closest bin (p = 0.12, paper_numbers section Q)
pooled sign test (22b)
bench: cVA on one antenna steers her 0.6-2.3 Hz towards it

edge_cases.description: Re-test the pooled lean after removing each female's own turning bias, and account for clustering and multiplicity.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: The raw index is mean(turn x sign(side)). A fly that turns one way regardless of the partner scores a 'lean' whenever the partner happens to sit mostly on that side. The paper already makes this argument for the published lobe (-0.19). Read-only prototype on the frozen logs: the hum female turns right (series mean turn -0.014 to -0.056; DNa R > L in every hum series), and the male sat on her right (mean side < 0) in 27 of 35 logs. The per-log index has the sign of (mean turn x mean side) in 27/35 mf and 22/22 ff logs.
edge_cases.how_to_run: New script experiments/lean_check.py. Args: --results (dir with encounter_trials.csv) and --chambers (default faint-smell,clean,noise0.2,noise0.2-virgin,rep-clean,rep-noise0.2,rep-noise0.2-virgin). For each female log of variant 'specific', take the pre-contact ticks within 6 blocks, as replication_stats.toward does. Compute: raw index; far-bias-corrected index mean((turn - b_far) * sign(az)), with b_far = mean ctl_turn over the log's non-contact ticks at near_dist >= 6; within-log side contrast 0.5*(mean turn | az>0 - mean turn | az<0) for logs with >= 10 ticks on each side; pre-contact tick count. Tests: two-sided sign test per pairing for each index; Holm across mf/ff; cluster sign tests over the 5 start configurations (t1..t5, all series share seed = trial number and the same start rotation) and over the 7 series. Output: experiments/results/lean_check.csv + .md. Run: $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 experiments/lean_check.py --results release/pre_rerun_20260926/results
edge_cases.pass_criterion: The lean is kept only if the far-bias-corrected mf sign test gives p < 0.025 (Holm over mf/ff) in the same direction. Prototype results: raw 24/9 (p = 0.0135); far-bias-corrected 15 towards / 20 away (p = 0.50); all-tick-bias-corrected 17/18 (p = 1.0); within-log side contrast 10/11 (n = 21, p = 1.0); configuration clusters 5/0 raw (p = 0.0625); series 5/2 (p = 0.45); Holm on the raw test 0.027. So the 'one trace' sentence (main text) and the pooled numbers in Note 9 should go, replaced by: the raw 24/9 is her right-turn bias times the side he happened to be on, and with her own turning subtracted there is no lean (15/20). Also fix the wording: 35 logs turn at all, 33 have a nonzero index.

edge_cases.description: The most sensitive in-world approach test. In the clean box the female walks straight on cVA with turn ~0 and the male stands still. Start her facing past him with a 1.6-block lateral offset (twice on each side, which cancels bias), plus one centred face-to-face control.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: If the bench's 0.6-2.3 Hz cVA steering acts in the world, she will curve in and touch him. Existing clean-mf contacts happen only in the face-to-face starts t1/t3 (both series), where walking straight is enough to hit him, so they cannot tell approach from geometry.
edge_cases.how_to_run: New code in experiments/trials.sh after the POS=(...) line: [ -n "${POS_SET:-}" ] && IFS=';' read -r -a POS <<< "$POS_SET". Entries are 'p1 p2 y1 y2', with fly1 the male. Use .5 decimals, because /tp centres integer coordinates (which is why '-2,64,0' logs as -1.5,0.5). With the server up: POS_SET='-1.5,64,0.5 2.5,64,2.1 -90 90;-1.5,64,0.5 2.5,64,-1.1 -90 90;2.5,64,0.5 -1.5,64,2.1 90 -90;2.5,64,0.5 -1.5,64,-1.1 90 -90;-1.5,64,0.5 2.5,64,0.5 -90 90' CONDS=mf NOISE=0 LABEL=offset-clean NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=3 caffeinate -i experiments/encounter_trials.sh 5 300. Then lean_check.py --chambers offset-clean, plus closest approach (min near_dist in the first 10 s of brain time) per log.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: 'No approach' holds if in the 4 offset trials the closest approach stays >= 1.4 blocks (the straight-line value is 1.6), there is no contact, and the bias-corrected index is within +-0.02, while the centred control touches. If she curves in (contact in >= 2/4, or closest approach below 1.6 on both sides), the pheromone steering is behaviour and Note 9 must say she approaches weakly.

claims.claim: Note 9 / 21b: the virgin female's acceptance neuron fires whether the male is near or far. She signals acceptance nearly 100 times a minute (99 and 91) yet never walks towards him (toward -0.005, +0.040).
already_tested: 5 + 5 trials; DNp37 15.8-16.6 Hz far / near / contact (tonic)
offline state arm: SAG -> pC1a-c, vpoDN
closest-bin per-log sign-flip p = 0.12
prototype bias-corrected virgin indices: 3 towards / 7 away across both series (no approach)

edge_cases.description: A virgin female with a courting male (P1 tonic), so that he actually sings. This is the strongest form of 'ready to say yes to anyone and walked towards no one'.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: In all virgin trials the male's P1/pIP10 sat at the hum floor, so she never heard song. Song reaches her as JO-A input and could change her speed or gate her acceptance.
edge_cases.how_to_run: With the server up: CONDS=mf STATE1=courting STATE2=virgin NOISE=0.2 LABEL=noise0.2-courting-virgin NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=3 caffeinate -i experiments/encounter_trials.sh 5 300 (STATE1 reaches fly1, the male, through run_pair.sh --state). Then encounter_stats.py --chamber noise0.2-courting-virgin and lean_check.py --chambers noise0.2-courting-virgin.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: The claim holds if DNp37 stays tonic and not distance-gated and the bias-corrected toward index stays within +-0.02 with the male singing. If acceptance becomes song- or distance-gated, or she approaches, the virgin paragraph changes. Caveats for the text: song in observe.js is non-directional (0/1 for 600 ms after any note), and JO-A drives her giant fibre (Note 4), so expect jumps. The '~100/min' is the decoder constant (0.1 events/s per Hz) times DNp37 ~16 Hz, and the male has no sense for it.

claims.claim: Note 10: the replication (25 new trials: clean at 300 s, hum and virgin at 600 s) reproduces. Clean females stood still, hum females met and stayed together, the male backed out of every meeting, and the virgin signalled acceptance to no one in particular.
already_tested: 25 trials under separate labels, side by side in replication_20260925.md and Table 1
discarded trials documented (sleep, memory stop)

edge_cases.description: Check that the body moves by brain time, not wall time, as bot.js intends ('a fly whose brain runs at 0.3x walks at 0.3x speed'), before comparing series run under different loads.
edge_cases.why_it_could_break: bot.js scales movement by an exponential average of past round trips (rtRatio) and keeps applying the last drive while the brain is stalled. Read-only prototype over all female logs: displacement per 50-ms brain step at walk ~0.6 is 0.034 blocks at 0.1-0.2 s wall gaps, 0.052 at 0.2-0.4, 0.10 at 0.8-1.6, 0.18 at 1.6-3.2 and 0.26 above 3.2 s. rep-clean mf ran with a median gap of 0.80 s and 50 % of rows > 0.8 s (originals 0.15-0.19 s, 0 %), so those bodies moved 2-5x farther per brain-second. rep-noise0.2 had 2.6 % stalled rows and rep virgin 3.8 %. Also, every series reuses seeds 1-5 with the same start rotation, so the noise-free clean replication is close to a replay rather than a new sample.
edge_cases.how_to_run: New script experiments/body_speed_check.py. For every arena log: gap = diff(t_wall), displacement = hypot(dx, dz) per row, and the previous row's ctl_walk. Bin gaps at 0.1/0.2/0.4/0.8/1.6/3.2 s and report displacement per unit walk per bin; per log report the share of rows with gap > 0.8 s, and flag logs above 5 %. Output: experiments/results/body_speed_check.csv. Run: $HOME/.pyenv/shims/python3 experiments/body_speed_check.py --results release/pre_rerun_20260926/results. Optional fix (new code): bot.js flag --freezeStale; in physics() use k = 0 while busy && Date.now() - sentAt > 4*TICK_MS.
edge_cases.pass_criterion: Cross-load comparisons are valid if displacement per brain step is flat across gap bins (top/bottom ratio < 1.3). The prototype gives ~5x, so Note 10 should say the loaded clean male-female replication is not comparable (rerun it as rep2-clean). The Methods should state a validity rule (< 5 % stalled rows, >= 60 s brain time). The hum-ff contact disagreement (11 vs 59 %) is not explained by load, since median gaps were similar (0.16-0.19 vs 0.19-0.26 s). sync-hum-ff settles it.

notes:
Five things the paper text disagrees with. I found them with read-only pandas analysis of the frozen encounter_trials.csv and the arena logs. The prototype scripts are in (scratch, not kept) (lean.py, lean2.py, start2.py, stall.py, bouts.py, pair2.py); nothing in the project was modified.

1. The pooled lean (Note 9, main text 'the one trace of it') does not survive removing the female's own turning bias. Raw 24/9 (p = 0.0135) becomes 15/20 (p = 0.50) with her far-field turn subtracted, 17/18 with the all-tick turn subtracted, and 10/11 within-log (n = 21). Other tests also weaken it:
   - Holm over the mf and ff tests gives 0.027.
   - Clustering by the 5 shared seed/start configurations gives 5/0 (p = 0.0625).
   - The test was chosen after looking: RESEARCH_NOTES 22b calls it 'found by pooling'.
   The mechanism is the hum female's rightward bias (DNa R > L in every hum series) times the male being on her right in 27/35 logs. The paper already uses this argument for the published-lobe -0.19. Minor: the script counts 35 logs that turn at all; 2 are exact zeros (clean t3, rep-clean t3), so '24 of the 33 that turn at all' is slightly misworded.

2. There is a launch-stagger bug in run_pair.sh (sleep 6 between the two bots). fly1's brain drives its body for 13-34 steps before fly2 exists; in ff trials fly1 walks 1-5 blocks in that time. In the face-to-face starts (t1, t3) this puts fly1 on fly2's spawn point. The headline 86.2-s bout (faint-smell off_ff_t3, Fig 3b) began at fly2's second tick after fly1 had walked 4.5 blocks. The flies never 'bumped into each other by chance'. Faint t1, rep-noise0.2 ff t1/t3 and published mf t1/t3 are the same. Without those trials: faint ff has 2/3 trials with contact and a longest genuine bout of 25.7 s; rep-noise0.2 ff has 3/3 and 26.9 s.

3. Body speed is not brain-time-invariant under load. Displacement per brain step grows about 5x with the wall gap, because rtRatio lags and the body keeps walking during brain stalls. rep-clean mf (median gap 0.8 s) is compromised; the rep hum and virgin series are only mildly affected.

4. Clean-box contacts (clean and rep-clean mf, 2/5 each) occur only in the face-to-face starts t1/t3. She walks straight on bilateral cVA, so these contacts are geometric, not approach. The paper's 'the flies start 4 blocks apart' hides that 2/5 starts face each other, 2/5 face away, and 1/5 is diagonal at 5.66 blocks.

5. On the hum, 'stayed together' is generous: median bout 0.3 s (orig) and 0.85 s (rep), with only 9-11 % of bouts over 5 s.

Independence:
- Both brains of a pair get the same --seed (run_pair.sh passes "$@" to both).
- Every series reuses seeds 1-5 with the same start rotation, so the 35 mf logs are 7 repeats of 5 configurations.
- In ff, both flies are counted, but they share contact ticks, so the Table 1 contact sd is over duplicated values (effective n = 5 pairs).
- I checked whether identical seeds correlate the two females: far-tick DNa correlation |r| <= 0.08. The RNG draw count per step depends on each brain's own sensory set, so the streams desync. It is not a practical problem, but separate seeds (SEED2 spec) are cheap hygiene.
- Note 8's 'jump in 12 % of moments' checks out (hum ff 12.6 %).

Script pitfalls for anyone running edge cases:
- LABEL must not contain '_'.
- encounter_trials.sh overwrites BRAIN_ARGS whenever NOISE != 0, so --gain and --seed cannot be combined with the hum through it; call trials.sh directly, and set NO_FOOD=1 VIEW1=0 VIEW2=0 by hand or the arena gets flowers, honey and cake.
- trials.sh hard-codes positions and seeds; POS_SET and SEED0 are new code.
- run_brain's log name does not record --gain.
- replication_stats.py's default --out overwrites experiments/results/replication_20260925.md, and --tex overwrites paper/tables_arena.tex. Always pass --out; never pass --tex for edge runs.
- encounter_stats.py rewrites experiments/results/encounter_trials.csv from all logs, so run it only after the offline re-run has finished.
- The frozen release copy lacks the noise_floor CSVs; they exist only in experiments/results.

Hardware plan:
- The guarded re-run queue is live: social-map was using ~6 GB with 9 % free at 23:54 (logs/guarded_mem.tsv). No arena run should start until it ends.
- Run the three analysis scripts first (< 2 min, < 0.5 GB each).
- Then make the code changes (SYNC, SEED0/SEED2, POS_SET) and run a 60-s smoke trial.
- Then run the arena steps one at a time, only when memory_pressure shows >= 50 % free (ff) or >= 55 % (mf).
- Set NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=3 explicitly. run_guarded.sh exports 6 and encounter_trials.sh inherits it, giving 12 threads for two brains.
- If using run_guarded.sh, discard any arena step with pauses > 0: SIGSTOP stops the bots and brains while the server keeps running, and the clients time out.

Server wrapper, run from the project root:
cd .; export PATH="$HOME/.pyenv/shims:$PATH"; (cd server && exec java -Xms512M -Xmx1536M -XX:+UseG1GC -jar paper.jar --nogui > ../logs/edge_server.out 2>&1) & SERVER=$!; for i in $(seq 1 120); do nc -z 127.0.0.1 25565 && break; sleep 5; done; sleep 20; <series commands>; kill -TERM $SERVER; wait $SERVER

Cost:
- Each 300-s trial takes about 6 minutes (300 s plus ~55 s overhead), so a 5-trial series is ~32 min and a 600-s series is ~57 min.
- Memory estimates (not measured for the arena; offline female steps peak at 1.4-1.5 GB, server heap is 1.5 GB): ff ~5.5 GB, mf ~7 GB, mm ~9 GB.
- Priority 1 and 2 simulations total ~3.2 h: sync-hum-ff 60 min, hum-level-ff 65, rep2-clean-mf 32, offset-facing-approach 32.
- Priority 3 adds 32 min each: male-male and courting-male-virgin.

Not worth the cost:
- Different starting distances: she walks straight, so distance only changes timing.
- Arena runs at gain 0.7 or 1.4: the offline gain sweep already predicts that male backing is lost at 0.7.
- A cVA-off control: the clean ff series already shows that a female's Or47b and CO2 move nothing, so the male's cVA is the only difference.
